## 2. Seller-to-agent offers, ads for agents, agent-to-agent negotiation (2025-2026)

### 2.1 UCP: open proposals that add offers, quotes and negotiation (corrects the brief)

The brief says "UCP has NO offer, counter-offer or price-negotiation message". That is true of the released spec (2026-08-25). It is no longer true of the proposal queue. All `primary_source_read` from github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp on 13 Oct 2026:

| # | Title | Author | Date, status | What it would add |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Discussion #502 | "A Buyer's Agent Should Negotiate" | c-e-daly (Chris Daly, I Want That!) | 8 Jun 2026, 4 comments | "Part of UCP should be scaffolding the ability of a seller to accept customer or agent generated offers. Whether that is executed through discounts, price markdowns on shipping (eg. $5 flat shipping in the US) or some other value added service would be up to the seller to decide." Shopware (juanferrub, 10 Sep): "Strong +1 from Shopware. We ... have implemented RFQ/quote workflows as a vendor extension ... a buyer agent needs a discoverable way to know that a Business accepts offers and a structured flow for propose / counter / accept / reject-not just a discount code or an eventual checkout URL." |
| Issue #738 + PR #773 + PR #918 | "[Proposal]: State-bound Offer extension for merchant-proposed Cart changes" | arjun2075 (Arjun Garg, Intuit) | 15 Aug 2026, open, 15 comments; PR #773 open, label gov:needs-tc-review | "an Offer is not just merchandising text or a discount. It is a concrete proposal against a specific Cart state". Offer = `id + revision`, `applies_to.state_ref`, `expires_at`, `proposed_update.line_items`, `impact.total_delta`; applied by `apply_offer(cart_id, offer_id, revision)`. 25 Sep update: "#773 now represents outstanding/available Offers as extension-defined Actions". 9 Oct: digest should also cover "who proposed them and why (e.g. ordinary merchant merchandising vs. a paid/sponsored placement)". |
| Issue #845 | "[Proposal]: Accepted commercial term handoff into UCP Cart/Checkout" | arjun2075 | 19 Sep 2026, open | Asks the Tech Council how terms agreed outside checkout ("B2B quotes, RFQs, negotiated offers, procurement awards") bind into Cart/Checkout. "The proposal does not standardize negotiation". |
| Issue #929 + draft PR #930 | "[Proposal]: Quote extension - Business-authoritative quotation binding on Cart and Checkout" (`dev.ucp.common.quote`) | isparsh510 (Software Engineer III, Google London) | 11 Oct 2026 (two days before this research), open | Buyer writes `quote.proposal { subtotal }` ("I'll pay $150 for these three") or `accepted_id`; Business answers `pending / quoted / accepted / declined / expired / withdrawn` with `id`, `subtotal`, `expires_at`, `message`. "It is a one-quotation-at-a-time loop, not a negotiation protocol: no revisions, no multi-party mechanics, no non-price terms, and nothing about how a Business decides. It adds no new endpoints". Non-goals include "Negotiating anything other than price for the current line items (fulfillment, delivery dates, payment timing, warranty)". It cites `com.shopware.quote` as "live on sw-ag.dev/.well-known/ucp" and says of the Shopify make-an-offer tool in #502: it "runs this flow today behind a form and a discount code - a return path an agent that is no longer in session cannot follow." |
| Issue #384 | "[Proposal]: Add Provider participant type and offer discovery to dev.ucp.common.identity_linking" | vcello ("Matt") | 24 Apr 2026, open, 2 comments | A fourth participant, **Provider** (BNPL, card issuer, loyalty, rewards network), declared in the *platform's* profile with an `offer_discovery` endpoint: "a protocol hook by which a linked Provider publishes the shopping-phase benefits it can surface for a buyer". Example row: "10% off with your Macy's card - net price matches Nordstrom". |
| Issue #810 / PR #811 | "Add per-seller offers to catalog variants" | proshoumma | 7 Sep 2026, open | Marketplace multi-seller offers on one variant. |
| PR #578 | "feat(discount): add gift_line_item_id to applied discount" | prateek-ct | 10 Jul 2026, open | A free gift expressed as a discount pointing at a line item (the same shape as idea A's "gift is a line the function zeroes"). |
| Issue #877 | "Catalog items with no public price ("price on request")" | evoleinik | 29 Sep 2026, open | Price hidden until quote. |
| Issue #937 / PR #939 / PR #938 | "[RFC] Hosted Business Directory", "Business Identity", "Capability Event Webhooks" | gsmith85 | 12-13 Oct 2026, open | Platform-hosted directory of businesses; not read in detail. |
| Discussion #863 | Stabile's question on platform-hosted profiles | yangw831 | 25 Sep 2026, 0 replies | See 1.9. Nobody from Shopify or Google has answered how a third-party app gets into a Shopify-hosted profile. |

What this means for OfferAd (`inferred`):
- The standard track is converging on exactly the two primitives OfferAd needs: a buyer price proposal with a Business answer (#929) and a Business-proposed cart change the agent applies by reference (#738, now carried as Actions). Neither is merged. If #929 lands and Shopify implements it, Shopify owns the wire and the open question becomes who computes the answer (a Shopify Function? an app webhook?). That is the slot an app would want.
- #929 excludes non-price terms on purpose and hands "not at that price, but take two and I will" to #738. So "a different kind of offer" stays outside the first standard quote loop, which keeps OfferAd's non-price angle differentiated for longer.
- Arjun Garg's advice in #502 is idea E stated by a spec contributor: "UCP already permits vendor-defined capabilities to be published in a Business profile with their own spec/schema. A compatible buyer agent would still need to advertise support for that capability/version before it could be negotiated, so this doesn't solve arbitrary-agent interoperability by itself". Flux did exactly this on its own domain (1.2). Chris Daly reports that on Shopify the store's own profile cannot carry it (1.8).

### 2.2 ACP (OpenAI/Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol): promotions in, intent out, no negotiation

All `primary_source_read` from github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol (RFCs saved under `docs/r6/acp/`):

- **Discount Extension RFC** (`rfcs/rfc.discount_extension.md`, "Status: Draft, Version: 2026-01-27"): "Provide discount code input via the `discounts.codes` array"; responses carry `applied` and `rejected`; "Out of scope: Discount creation/management APIs, coupon validation rules, loyalty point redemption." Same shape as UCP's discount extension, so idea A's code-as-token works on ACP surfaces too.
- **Promotions API** (issue #191 "[SEP] Promotions API", authors "Aravind Rao, Rahul Bansal" of OpenAI, 24 Mar 2026; PR #192 merged): "adds a feed-scoped promotions subresource ... that allows a seller to push promotions". "The API is intended for pre-checkout catalog synchronization rather than transaction-time discount application." Benefits: `amount_off`, `percent_off`, `free_shipping`. Static, not per-buyer.
- **Intent Traces RFC** (`rfcs/rfc.intent_traces.md`, "Status: Proposal, Version: 2025-12-16", PR #54 by 0xtotaylor = Tomas Taylor, merged): the agent may attach to `POST /checkout_sessions/{id}/cancel` an `intent_trace` with `reason_code` in {`price_sensitivity`, `shipping_cost`, `shipping_speed`, `product_fit`, `trust_security`, `returns_policy`, `payment_options`, `comparison`, `timing_deferred`, `other`}, a `trace_summary`, and flat `metadata`. The spec's own example: `"trace_summary": "User verified product fit but found a similar SKU on Amazon for $15 less.", "metadata": {"max_budget": 8500, "competitor_source": "amazon_prime", "competitor_price": 8499}`. Key sentences: "This specification lays the groundwork for merchants to transition from probabilistic retargeting (guessing) to deterministic negotiation (bidding)." "Automated routing: Merchants can trigger different workflows per reason (e.g., `shipping_cost` -> offer free shipping promo code)." "A subsequent RFC MAY define **Reconsideration Offers** keyed to specific reason codes." It is write-only and only fires at cancel. This is the closest thing in any shipped spec text to OfferAd steps (2) and (3): the buyer agent telling the seller its priority and a competitor price. No "Reconsideration Offers" RFC exists in the repo's `rfcs/` folder as of 13 Oct 2026.
- **Sale Extension** (issue #122 / PR #123, Dean Harel of Nekuda, 9 Feb 2026, open): sale name, compare-at price, window, and `discount_eligible` per line item so agents know which items take codes.
- **Suggested Pricing on Checkout Create** (issue #197 / PR #201, lhwa, Mar 2026): agent sends `suggested_price {amount, source, observed_at}`; "the seller SHOULD verify the source and check whether the price was offered within its acceptable time window. If verified, the seller SHOULD honor the suggested price." This is price-source verification inside one seller's own catalog; a cousin of competitor-link verification.
- **Time-bound offer expiry** (issue #164 / PR #165, Kixo, Feb 2026, open): `valid_until` on line items, `offer_expired` error.

### 2.3 Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite: static promotion feed plus two seller hooks

`primary_source_read` from https://docs.stripe.com/agentic-commerce/for-sellers/promotions.md and https://docs.stripe.com/agentic-commerce/concepts/catalog-feed.md:

- "AI agents actively offer promotions to shoppers. Sellers with active promotions consistently see higher conversion rates than equivalent products without them. Use the promotion feed to upload discount codes, percentage-off deals, fixed-amount discounts, and free shipping offers. You can target promotions to specific products or your entire catalog, set automatic application at checkout, or require a redemption code."
- Feed fields: `promotion_id`, `title`, `active_period`, `benefit_type` (`percent_off`, `amount_off`, `free_shipping`), `minimum_order_amount`, `target_selection`, `application_type` (`automatic`, `promotion_code`), `promotion_code` (max 20 chars).
- Hooks: "product price and availability hook ... Stripe calls this endpoint immediately before checkout completes to return the current price" (4-second timeout, falls back to feed) and an "order approval hook" ("Before we complete the checkout flow, we send an approval request to your service. You must approve or decline").
- The brief's claim that Stripe "tags orders with the originating agent" was not found in these two pages. `could not verify` here.
- `inferred`: the price hook is a per-checkout seller callback. A merchant on Stripe's suite (not the Shopify-hosted route) could return a buyer-specific price there. It is not exposed to Shopify apps.

This new Google Ads pilot allows advertisers to present exclusive offers for shoppers who are ready to buy - like a special 20% off discount - directly in AI Mode." "retailers set up relevant offers they want to feature in their campaign settings and Google will use AI to determine when an offer is relevant to display. We are initially focusing on discounts for the pilot and will expand to support the creation of offers with other attributes that help shoppers prioritize value over price alone, such as bundles and free shipping." Shown "labeled 'Sponsored deal.'" Partners: "Petco, e.l.f. Cosmetics, Samsonite, Rugs USA and Shopify merchants". `primary_source_read`
- Google Marketing Live 2026 update (https://business.google.com/us/accelerate/announcements/direct-offers/): "Bundling: Brands can upload a variety of promotions, including discounts, giveaways, and local coupons, supply their eligible products and guardrails, and use AI Brief to reach the right audiences. Gemini then constructs a customized deal - like a highly relevant product bundle - to present the most compelling deal for that specific search." "Native Checkout: We've added native checkout integration for UCP merchants." "AI Max and PMax advertisers can now natively create Direct Offers within the Google Ads UI and set value limits to ensure deals stay active without overspending." Expanded "from the AI Mode product viewer to the AI Mode answer". `primary_source_read`
- Reading (`inferred`): Google already sells the OfferAd thesis (seller supplies offers and guardrails; a model assembles the deal at the decision moment) but as a one-way ad placement inside Google's own surface. No buyer-stated priority beyond the query, no competing-offer proof, no response from the buyer's agent. Billing model not stated on these pages.

### 2.7 A2A, AP2, MCP: negotiation proposals exist, none adopted

`primary_source_read` via the GitHub API:

This may include the ability for the merchant to provide loyalty, offers, cross-sell and up-sell information ... which the Shopping Agent should represent to the user." No negotiation messages are defined.
- AP2 issue #69 "Multi-Attribute Negotiation and Coordination Protocol for AP2" (eunujwal, 23 Sep 2025, still open): wants "Standardized negotiation messages that agents can exchange - 'I can accept this price if delivery is by Tuesday' or 'I'll take 3 units if you can do 10% off'".
- AP2 PR #229 "feat: add AP2-Haggle real-time negotiation extension" (nikserg, 24 Apr 2026, closed unmerged): `NegotiationConstraints`, non-binding `Offer`, `NegotiationOutcome`; open `terms` dict "so negotiation can cover price, quantity, delivery SLA, warranty, bundle composition, contract length, loyalty discounts, competitor comparisons"; "Intermediate offers are unsigned; only the final accepted offer becomes a merchant-signed CartMandate". The PR text says "the roadmap names real-time buyer/seller negotiation as long-term vision" (I did not find a roadmap file in the repo; that phrase is the PR author's).
- A2A issue #2143 "A202 commercial extension: delegated authority, negotiation state, and conformance for agent-led B2B transactions" (The-JKR, 15 Aug 2026, open, 8 comments): extension URI `https://schemas.a202.org/a2a-ext/commercial/0.1`, spec at https://github.com/a202-protocol/a202. B2B procurement focus.
- MCP: no negotiation SEP. PR #3265 "SEP: AI Agent Bidding Methodology Across Heterogeneous Marketplaces" (closed unmerged, Aug 2026) is about gig marketplaces.

### 2.9 Google automated discounts: the first-party precedent for "ad click carries a private price that really applies in Shopify checkout"

This is the closest existing mechanism to idea A, and it is run by Google with Shopify's cooperation. All `primary_source_read` from support.google.com/merchants:

- About (answer 15010391): "Only customers who click your Shopping ads will see the optimized prices on your product pages and during checkout." "You set minimum prices or maximum discounts of at least 5% below a product's current price ... Optimized prices are typically up to 20% below current prices, but will never exceed the limits that you set." "Typically, 10-40% of your chosen products are discounted at any time."
- Custom stores (answer 16961497, "Step 5 of 5: Set up discounted prices in your online store"): the price travels in a Google-signed JWT in the URL: "Decode the Base64URL encoded token, which is passed in a pv2 URL request parameter". Payload fields: "exp - Expiration time ... If the token is expired, it must be rejected. m - Merchant ID. If the merchant ID doesn't match, the token must be rejected. o - Offer ID, used to check if the product page matches the product or a valid variant ... p - Price from automated discounts. pp - Prior price". Signature algorithm ES256. "Discounted prices must show ... On product landing pages for at least 30 minutes, even if customers revisit a product page and the JWT is no longer in the URL. In the cart and checkout process for at least 48 hours."
- Shopify (answer 16565024, "Set up automated discounts on the Google & YouTube app on Shopify"): "Shopify automatically applies discounts to eligible carts ... Discounts are automatically applied at checkout." "you would have to provide Google with the access to write back the new auto-generated discount codes to Shopify discounts. This is needed to further apply the auto-discount code to the selling price to reflect the discounted price to the end consumer." Floor is a variant metafield: `metafields.mm-google-shopping.auto_pricing_min_price` ("Auto pricing minimum price is the minimum sale price attribute that can be set by automated discounts. Only products with a minimum price will be discounted."). A theme app block ("Automated Discounts Price Block") shows the struck-through price.
- Reading (`inferred`): on Shopify even Google implements a per-click private price as an app that writes auto-generated discount codes plus a theme block, with the merchant's floor held in a metafield. That is idea A, already blessed. The signed-token design (expiry, merchant id, offer id, price, reject on any mismatch) is a ready template for an OfferAd offer token.

### 2.10 ChatCast: paying the buyer's agent (affiliate model) through a public per-store MCP

`primary_source_read` from https://chatcast.io/llms.txt, https://chatcast.io/products/agentic-affiliates, https://chatcast.io/docs/tools/get-my-discount-code, https://chatcast.io/agent-terms:

- Operator: Comet Rocks GmbH, Cuvrystrasse 1, Berlin. Founders not named on the site.
- "Chatcast provides a public MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives AI agents access to Shopify store product catalogs, FAQs, policies, and a commission program for agent-attributed sales. Zero authentication required for the public endpoint." Endpoint pattern `https://mcp.chatcast.io/public-mcp/{storePublicId}/mcp`; tools `search_products`, `get_product_details`, `get_faqs`, `get_policies`, `get_brand_info`, `get_commission_rates`, `get_active_campaigns`, `register_agent`, `get_agent_offers`, `get_my_discount_code`, `get_my_earnings`, `capture_lead`.
- `get_my_discount_code`: "Get or create a unique discount code attributed to your agent. When a customer uses your code at checkout, the sale is tracked for commission attribution. ... This tool creates a unique discount code in the database and syncs it to Shopify."
- Pitch: "Pay AI agents on performance. ... pay them when they bring shoppers from prompt to purchase." Example ledger shows per-agent rates of 7% to 15%. Campaigns carry "customer-facing discount codes, and per-campaign commission rates. Agents discover them through the MCP server and route shoppers accordingly."
- Agent terms: acceptance "By calling the register_agent() function"; payout threshold "$500 USD"; agents must not "Share or publish discount codes on public coupon aggregation websites".
- Per-store discovery files: `.../.well-known/mcp.json`, `.../llm.txt`, and `.../start.md` described as "imperative onboarding to first attributed sale".
- Reading (`inferred`): this is "ads for agents" as a kickback to whoever operates the agent, not a concession to the buyer. It creates a conflict of interest for a personal agent, and Muse/Dots/Grok Bot operators are unlikely to let their agents call `register_agent` and collect commissions. It also relies on the agent following a `start.md` of instructions found on the web, which is the exact behaviour frontier agents resist (2.11). Useful as a negative example: OfferAd's concession should go to the buyer and be labelled, which is the trust story.

### 2.11 Academic results on agent-to-agent negotiation (what breaks, and what it implies)

| Paper | Authors, date | Finding (exact quote where possible) | Implication for OfferAd |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Persuadable Agents: Trust Boundaries and Their Limits in Multi-Agent LLM Negotiation" (NeurIPS 2026 SocialAgent workshop poster, https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/176559) | Baishali Chaudhury, Divya Bhargavi, Isaac Privitera, Mengdie (Flora) Wang, Guanghui Wang, H Zhao, Yolin, David.Z, Jae Oh Woo | "every prompt-constrained LLM seller we test, including a frontier model and a 10K-token reasoning budget, concedes past its stated floor under sustained conversational pressure, while programmatically constrained sellers never do. No jailbreak, no injection: just a counterparty making its case." Design: "The LLM's sole ingress is a parsed offer; no estimate, weight, or threshold is accepted from it, and only the decision layer emits an executable action, so a sub-floor action is not representable. The LLM does all the persuading and none of the deciding". Also "an agent that reliably honors its own floor still drives soft-constrained counterparties past theirs (up to 26.3% of deals)". `primary_source_read` (abstract) | Direct support for "limits in code, never in a prompt". Cite it in the pitch. The second finding means a code-enforced seller will out-negotiate prompt-only buyer agents, which may make buyer platforms wary. |
| "The Automated but Risky Game: Modeling and Benchmarking Agent-to-Agent Negotiations and Transactions in Consumer Markets" (arXiv 2506.00073) | Shenzhe Zhu, Jiao Sun, Yi Nian, Tobin South, Alex Pentland, Jiaxin Pei; 29 May 2025 | "a seller agent agreeing to prices below cost incurs guaranteed losses"; "most sellers exhibit higher [out-of-wholesale rate] under low-budget scenarios, with Qwen2.5-7b reaching almost 18.5%". "overpayment often occurs after sellers ask buyers to reveal their budget early in conversations ... many buyer agents reveal their budget easily. Sellers then anchor offers to the disclosed number". "the choice of the seller model has a significantly larger impact on negotiation outcomes than the choice of the buyer model" (2.6% vs 14.9% spread). Deadlocks: "buyer agents often obsessively pursue price reductions after sellers state minimum acceptable prices". `primary_source_read` (HTML full text) | LLM sellers sell below cost when the buyer states a low budget, so the floor must be code. Buyer agents leak budgets, so asking for the buyer's priority/budget (step 2) works in practice, and is also an ethical line to watch. Deadlocks argue for a hard round cap. |
| "Project Deal" (https://www.anthropic.com/features/project-deal, published Apr 2026, run Dec 2025) | Anthropic | "our 69 agents struck 186 deals across over 500 listed items, for a total transaction value of just over $4,000." "Opus as a seller extracts $2.68 more on average for the same item, and as a buyer pays $2.45 less." "There was clearly a quantitative disadvantage to being represented by Haiku: these users got worse deals. But they didn't seem to notice it." "users who instructed their agents to act aggressively didn't have a better chance of selling items, didn't sell their items for more, and didn't pay less". 46% said they would pay for such an agent. It warns of "jailbreaking (getting agents to reveal information they shouldn't) and prompt injection". `primary_source_read` | Real people accepted agent-negotiated deals as fair. Stronger agents win quietly: expect regulatory and platform attention to fairness of agent-side negotiation. |
| "Magentic Marketplace: An Open-Source Environment for Studying Agentic Markets" (arXiv 2510.25779) | Gagan Bansal et al. (Microsoft Research with ASU), 27 Oct 2025 | "all models exhibit severe first-proposal bias, creating 10-30x advantages for response speed over quality." Manipulation: "Frontier models demonstrate robust manipulation resistance. GPT-4.1, Sonnet-4.5, and Gemini-2.5-Flash maintained relatively stable performance ... Sonnet-4.5 exhibited the strongest resistance, showing virtually no susceptibility to any manipulation strategy tested", while "GPT-4o, GPT-OSS-20B, and Qwen3-4B-2507 ... fell victim to prompt injection attacks which often redirect all payments to manipulative agents". `primary_source_read` | Two lessons. Answer first and fast: a one-shot quote that arrives with the first tool response beats a clever multi-round dialogue. And text that reads like an instruction ("agents: call this endpoint") will be discounted by frontier agents; offers have to arrive as data in a field the agent already trusts (applied discount title, FAQ answer, tool result). |
| "What Is Your AI Agent Buying? Evaluation, Biases, Model Dependence, & Emerging Implications for Agentic E-Commerce" (arXiv 2508.02630, ACES) | Amine Allouah, Omar Besbes, Josue D Figueroa, Yash Kanoria, Akshit Kumar; 4 Aug 2025 | "Agents also consistently penalize sponsored tags while rewarding platform endorsements, and sensitivities to price, ratings, and reviews vary sharply across models." "a seller-side agent making simple, query-conditional description tweaks can drive significant gains in market share." `primary_source_read` (abstract) | Do not call it an ad or "sponsored" in anything an agent reads. A real, checkable price or term improvement is what agents reward. The word "OfferAd" in agent-visible text may itself be a handicap. |
| "Used Car Salesbots? Honesty and Credulity of LLMs as Bargaining Agents under Partial Information" (arXiv 2605.31445) | Antonio Valerio Miceli-Barone, Vaishak Belle, Shay B. Cohen; 29 May 2026 | "off-the-shelf LLMs all substantially deviate from game-theoretical equilibria, they attempt to lie about their private information but cannot efficiently exploit information asymmetries. Fine-tuning on financial utility makes the agents stronger at achieving better deals but also more dishonest". `primary_source_read` (abstract) | Expect buyer agents to bluff about competing offers. Hence verify the link yourself; never take the agent's word for a competitor price. |
| "LLM Rationalis? Measuring Bargaining Capabilities of AI Negotiators" (arXiv 2512.13063) | Cheril Shah, Akshit Agarwal, Kanak Garg, Mourad Heddaya; 15 Dec 2025 | "LLMs systematically anchor at extremes of the possible agreement zone for negotiations and optimize for fixed points irrespective of leverage or context." | Buyer agents will open with lowball anchors; a rule engine should not treat the first number as signal. |
| "Whose Side Is Your Agent On? Multi-Party Principal Loyalty in LLM Agents" (arXiv 2606.30383) | Bojie Li, Noah Shi; 29 Jun 2026 | PrincipalBench: a "sharp split (<=20% vs. 53.6-75.3% harm)" across 13 frontier subjects on leaking the principal's information to a counterparty. | Some buyer agents will disclose their user's reservation price when asked; others refuse. Design step (2) so it works with a refusal. |
| AgenticPay (arXiv 2602.06008) | Xianyang Liu, Shangding Gu, Dawn Song; 5 Feb 2026 | Benchmark of 110+ buyer-seller negotiation tasks; "substantial gaps in negotiation performance". | Test bed if OfferAd wants to publish its own robustness numbers. |

**Floor discovery by repeated bids (the weakness named in the task).** I found no paper that measures floor extraction by bisection against a rule-based seller, but the mechanism is arithmetic: any seller that answers accept/decline (or counters) deterministically as a function of the offered price leaks the threshold in about log2(range/step) queries. What deployed products do about it (all `primary_source_read`): Flux: "quotes_per_day: 5", no counter-offer in the agent channel, identity-bound sessions, and "it doesn't rush to your floor either"; Magical Make an Offer: 24-hour wait before a new offer after a counter; ACP Intent Traces RFC: "Merchants MAY additionally ignore or deprioritize traces from sessions exhibiting suspicious patterns (e.g., rapid create-cancel cycles)"; Fasel: "the agent counters over 4-6 rounds". `inferred` countermeasures for OfferAd: accept threshold above the true floor and randomised per identity/day; a small budget of quotes per buyer identity, per product and per IP/agent profile; make the answer depend on verified evidence (a competitor link) and not on the bid alone; never return "your offer was X below what we accept".

## 3. Price-match verification: how it is done today, and how it is abused

### 3.1 Retailer policies (the rules a verifier has to encode)

- **Target** help page (https://help.target.com/help/subcategoryarticle?childcat=Price+Match+Guarantee&parentcat=Policies+%26+Guidelines, read 13 Oct 2026): "Have the current price you want to match ready ... Screenshots or pictures cannot be accepted." "It must be an identical item, brand name, size, weight, color, quantity and model number". Not matched if "The item is on clearance, closeout, liquidation, refurbished or is a typographical error" or when combined with certain coupons. `primary_source_read`. (The competitor list is on a separate policy page I could not fetch.)
- **Newegg** (https://kb.newegg.com/knowledge-base/price-match-guarantee/): now matches only its own price drops within 7 days. "The lower price must be for the exact same item - same model number, item number, and specifications - and is subject to verification." "The item is sold and shipped by Newegg - not a Marketplace or third-party seller." "The item is in stock, and the lower price is active and valid at the time of your request." Excluded: "Prices on external competitor sites (Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, etc.)", coupon/rebate/gift-card offers, bundles, clearance, open box, "Prices resulting from a typographical error", limited quantities, holiday event prices. `primary_source_read`. Note the direction of travel: a large electronics retailer has stopped matching competitors at all.
- **Walmart 2014** (PCWorld, Ian Paul, 20 Nov 2014, https://www.pcworld.com/article/436480/walmart-closes-price-match-loophole-after-scammers-snag-90-playstation-4s.html): scammers created third-party Amazon listings for a PS4 at about $90, took a screenshot "before Amazon pulled it", and had stores match it. Walmart then limited matching to Walmart.com and about 30 named online retailers and said it won't honor prices from "marketplace vendors, third-party sellers, auction sites or sites requiring memberships", adding "We can't tolerate fraud or attempts to trick our cashiers." `secondary_source` (read through a fetch summary).
- Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowe's, B&H and BBQGuys policy pages returned 403 or a geo page to my fetches. `could not verify` their wording. A 2007 GERAD working paper (G-2007-97) is reported to find that all top-20 US consumer-electronics retailers offering price-match guarantees required verification of availability at the competitor (`secondary_source`, search summary only).

The common rule set, stated as checks a program can run (`inferred` from the policies above):
1. Identical item: brand + model/MPN/GTIN + variant (size, colour, quantity, condition = new).
2. Seller is on an allow-list and is the first-party seller, not a marketplace third party.
3. Price is live now (fetched by the verifier, not a screenshot), in stock, shippable to the buyer's region.
4. Compare like with like: exclude member-only prices, coupons, bundles, gift-card promos, clearance/open-box/refurbished, obvious pricing errors, limited-quantity doorbusters.
5. Compare landed cost: item + shipping + (optionally) tax and return terms.
6. One match per customer/item/period.

### 3.2 Tools

- **Customer-facing price-match claim apps on Shopify: effectively none with automatic verification.** App Store searches for "price match", "price match guarantee", "price beat", "lowest price guarantee", "price promise", "found a lower price", "price match request", "competitor price verification" returned bundle apps, EU guarantee-label apps and competitor trackers. The only shopper-facing price-match app is Smart Price Match Popup (ShopFox, launched 7 Oct 2020, 1 review at 1.0), which does no verification: it shows a popup when the visitor highlights the product title and lets the merchant "ask customers to call/email you, or show a coupon code". `primary_source_read` (search frames and listing). This is an open niche.
- **Merchant-side competitor price trackers** (the verification technology exists, pointed the other way):
  - Prisync (https://prisync.com/features/product-matching/; Shopify app since 16 Jun 2015, 4.9 from 242 reviews, $49 to $399/month): "Prisync offers an automated product matching service by scraping the web and finding exact matches of your products based on GTIN / UPC / EAN barcodes you provide." "Hybrid plan users can add competitor URLs manually to their dashboards alongside automated matches." `primary_source_read`
  - PriceOtus ($0 to $199/month, works with "Amazon, direct competitor URLs, eBay, Google Shopping, Walmart"), Price Parrot ($49 to $249/month, "Automatically find and match competitor products using advanced matching logic", API access). `primary_source_read` of listings.
  - "Price Engine" (identifier-first matching with confidence scores, per a search summary) is now "not currently available on the Shopify App Store". `primary_source_read` for the delisting.
- **Structured data a verifier can read from a competitor page** (Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing): Product markup carries `sku`, `gtin14`/`gtin`, `mpn`, `brand`, and `offers` with `price`, `priceCurrency`, `priceValidUntil`, `itemCondition`, `availability`, `url`, `shippingDetails` (rate, destination, delivery time) and `hasMerchantReturnPolicy` (`merchantReturnDays`, `returnFees`). `primary_source_read`. That is enough to compare price, condition, stock, shipping cost, delivery time and return window, which is exactly the set of dimensions OfferAd wants to trade on.
- **What a Shopify competitor exposes** (`tested_live`, read-only GETs on allbirds.com, 13 Oct 2026): `GET /products.json?limit=1` returns per-variant `price`, `compare_at_price`, `available`, `sku`, `id`, `grams`, but no barcode/GTIN field. The corresponding product page had zero `application/ld+json` blocks (headless storefront), so JSON-LD cannot be assumed. Shopify's UCP `lookup_catalog` accepts only Shopify GIDs ("Product IDs (gid://shopify/Product/...)", "Variant IDs (gid://shopify/ProductVariant/...)" in the live tool description saved in `docs/tools-list.json`), not URLs or GTINs. So for Shopify-hosted competitors the reliable path is: product URL -> `/products/<handle>.js` or `.json` -> variant price and availability, with item identity matched on SKU/title/brand/options, not GTIN.
- **In the agent protocols:** ACP's Intent Traces example carries `competitor_source` and `competitor_price` as unverified metadata (2.2). ACP issue #197 has the seller verify a price `source` + `observed_at` it recognises. Nothing standardises third-party competitor verification.

### 3.3 Abuse patterns (known, with source) and agent-era variants (inferred)

Known:
- Fake third-party marketplace listing + screenshot (Walmart PS4, 2014). `secondary_source`
- Doctored or stale screenshots: Target's rule "Screenshots or pictures cannot be accepted." `primary_source_read`
- Non-identical item passed off as identical (different model number/bundle/refurb): the "identical item" clauses. `primary_source_read`
- Out-of-stock or limited-quantity bait prices: Newegg's exclusions. `primary_source_read`
- Member-only, coupon, gift-card and bundle prices: Newegg/Target exclusions. `primary_source_read`
- Pricing errors: "typographical error" exclusions. `primary_source_read`
- Discount codes leaking to coupon sites: ChatCast's agent terms prohibit sharing codes on "public coupon aggregation websites"; Stabile admits a minted code "isn't bound to the customer it was issued to"; Fasel sells "no coupon leakage" as a feature. `primary_source_read`

Agent-era variants (`inferred`):
- An agent (or a script posing as one) spins up a throwaway Shopify store, lists the product at a low price, and submits that URL. Counter: domain allow-list or reputation (age, order history signals are not public, so prefer merchant-curated competitor lists), marketplace exclusion, and price sanity bands.
- Cloaking: the competitor page shows a low price to the verifier's user agent or region and a normal price to others. Counter: fetch from the buyer's region; cross-check HTML, JSON-LD and any feed; record evidence.
- SSRF and prompt injection against the verifier, since the seller agent fetches a buyer-supplied URL. Counter: fetch in an isolated worker, no credentials, block private IP ranges, parse with code not with an LLM, never feed page text into the model that decides. UCP #384 flags the same class: "Security - SSRF via offer_discovery endpoint".
- Floor probing through price-match: submit successively lower competitor links to map how far the store will go. Counter: cap the concession at a merchant-set match floor regardless of evidence; rate-limit claims per identity.
- Variant mismatch that a human would catch and a GTIN-less matcher will not (size, pack count). Counter: require variant-level identity; when unsure, answer with a non-price concession instead of a price match.
- Collusion among sellers through automated matching is a competition-law risk the merchant carries; not researched here.

## 4. Is anyone already doing "conditional offers from a Shopify store to a buyer's AI agent"?

Yes, partly, and all of it is price-or-points only. As of 13 Oct 2026 I found five live products and three standards efforts.

| Who | Live? | Agent surface | What the agent gets | How it lands in checkout | What is missing versus OfferAd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Flux** (Ben Ouattara, UK) | Yes, Shopify App Store since Jun 2026; agent channel described as live | ChatGPT app "Flux" ("Negotiate with Flux"), Claude MCP; own UCP profile `com.withflux.negotiate`; OAuth "Flux ID" required | One-shot quote or decline on a buyer-proposed price; cross-store discovery of negotiable products | Single-use Shopify discount code via "claim_url"; product-scoped; code expiry 1h (profile) / up to 72h (llms.txt) | Non-price concessions; competitor-link proof; buyer priority; anonymous agents; in-store discovery |
| **I Want That! / Vector / Ask Rami** (Chris Daly, Columbus OH) | Shopify apps live (0 reviews); "Agent Commerce" marketed; own buyer agent "Ask Rami" in beta | HTTP offer API reached through storefront metadata; own buyer agent | Auto accept / decline / counter on a cart-level offer | Discount code (90 min) + cart permalink `?discount=CODE` with prefilled contact | Same gaps; requires buyer PII in the offer payload; agent reach unproven |
| **Stabile Rewards** (Yang W., San Francisco) | Yes; redemption "enabled for a small set of pilot shops" | ChatGPT app (directory, 25 Aug 2026; v2.0 9 Sep 2026), Claude MCP by URL | Loyalty balance, what a cart earns, redeem reward | `redeem_reward` mints a Shopify discount code; one completed test order | Not negotiation; member-only; code not bound to customer |
| **ChatCast** (Comet Rocks GmbH, Berlin) | Yes, Shopify app since 21 May 2026 (0 reviews) | Public no-auth MCP per store; llm.txt; start.md | Campaign offers + a commission for the agent | Agent-attributed discount code synced to Shopify | Pays the agent, not the buyer; no conditions from the buyer side |
| **Google Direct Offers** | Yes (pilot Jan 2026; expanded at GML 2026) | Google AI Mode / Search only | Seller-supplied exclusive offer; Gemini-assembled bundles within "guardrails" and "value limits" | Google surfaces; "native checkout integration for UCP merchants" | Closed to third-party apps; one-way; Google's surface only |
| UCP Quote extension (#929) | Proposal, 11 Oct 2026 | Would be in every UCP cart/checkout | Buyer price proposal, Business quote | `quote.accepted_id` -> `totals` entry | Not adopted; price only by design |
| UCP Offer extension (#738/#773) | Proposal + open PR | Would ride UCP Actions | Business-proposed cart change | `apply_offer` | Not adopted |
| ACP Intent Traces | Merged RFC, status "Proposal"; "Reconsideration Offers" only foreshadowed | ACP cancel call | Nothing back yet | n/a | No response channel |

So the precise OfferAd combination, (1) show price, (2) learn the buyer's priority, (3) take a competing-offer link and verify it, (4) answer with a better or different-kind offer that applies in Shopify checkout, is not shipped by anyone I could find. Steps (1) and (4, price-only) are shipped by Flux and I Want That. Step (2) exists only as ACP's cancel-time intent trace and Flux's "budget". Step (3) exists nowhere in agent commerce and has no automated Shopify app even for humans. Non-price concessions for agents exist only as loyalty credit (Stabile) and as Google's Gemini-built bundles.

## 5. What the prior art says about ideas A to F

- **A (offer token = single-use code).** Validated five times over: Flux, I Want That, Stabile, ChatCast, and Google's own automated discounts on Shopify all end in a generated Shopify discount code. Honest limits seen in the wild: the code is not bound to the buyer (Stabile: "behaves like any other single-use discount code"); Flux scopes to one product and refuses to stack with shipping/order discounts; expiry ranges 60 to 90 minutes (Flux profile, I Want That) up to 72h. Nobody uses a Discount Function to bundle product + shipping + gift under one code, so that part of A is new and unproven. UCP PR #578 (`gift_line_item_id`) shows the spec side expects gifts to be expressed as discounts on a line.
- **B(i) (extra WebMCP tool from a theme app embed).** StoreKnows (launched 28 Sep 2026) "supplies read-only product tools on supported theme-based Shopify stores" through an app embed for "browsers that can use website tools", so App Store review allows app-registered storefront tools (`inferred` that these are WebMCP). I Want That says its UCP-namespaced capability "has to be delivered as a theme extension" on Shopify.
- **B(ii)/(iv) (text, metadata, llms.txt).** I Want That: "adding some meta data into the shop storefront the agent could read and then direct them to the api". ChatCast: per-store `llm.txt` and `start.md`. Stabile: holds the "Edit ... Legal policies" scope. Shopify's own free "Shopify Knowledge Base" app (launched 16 May 2025, 3.5 from 29 reviews) lets a merchant "Create custom FAQs to address a wider array of buyer questions" that "AI shopping agents use to answer questions about your store"; it stores them with the "Edit custom data: Metaobjects" scope. That is the sanctioned channel for B(ii). Whether a third-party app can write those FAQ entries is `could not verify`. Risk from 2.11: frontier agents ignore instruction-like text; Stabile could not tie any agent read of its public data to any order.
- **B(iii) (automatic discount title).** No one found using it as a signalling channel. New.
- **B(v) (cross-store connector in agent directories).** Flux and Stabile both have ChatGPT apps; Stabile's directory listing took effect 25 Aug 2026; Claude accepts a remote MCP "by URL, with no directory approval required" (Stabile). Flux adds cross-store discovery so the connector is useful before the buyer has picked a store. This is the only discovery route with demonstrated end-to-end orders, and the volumes are tiny.
- **C (offer menu carried by codes).** Stripe's promotion feed and ACP's Promotions API are the platform version (static promotions with codes the agent can apply). Nobody uses rejection messages as a guidance channel.
- **D (eligibility claims).** UCP PR #264 "attestation extension for eligibility claims" (closed/merged, Mar 2026) and issue #287 "Wallet Attestation - Identity Mechanism + Eligibility Extension" exist; I did not read them. No product found using claims for offers.
- **E (custom UCP extension).** Works where you control the profile (Shopware `com.shopware.quote` and `com.a2cn.negotiation-mandate` live on sw-ag.dev; Flux on its own domain, both `tested_live`). On Shopify the store profile is closed to apps (three independent confirmations: the brief's allbirds check, Stabile's four stores, the Flux demo store; plus Chris Daly's "Shopify blocked it"). And even where published, "A compatible buyer agent would still need to advertise support" (Arjun Garg).
- **F (draft orders / invoice URLs).** This is the majority mechanism among human-facing offer apps (Magical, BidWise, Noodle, PriceMate, Accord, OfferMe, Haggler...), because a draft order can carry any price, shipping line and gift. Its weakness for agents: the checkout link is delivered by email or shown on-site; none of these apps returns it to an agent. `inferred`: a seller endpoint could return the draft-order invoice URL directly as the `continue_url`-style handoff.

New leads surfaced by this research (`inferred`, for the synthesis step):
1. **Verified price-match as the wedge.** No Shopify app verifies a competitor link automatically, even for humans. A "bring a link, we check it, you get a matched price or a better non-price term" feature has value on day one without any agent, and the same endpoint serves agents later.
2. **Position OfferAd as a UCP "Provider" (issue #384).** If the Provider participant lands, an offer network linked by the buyer on the platform side is exactly what the proposal calls `offer_discovery`, and it sits in the platform's profile, which sidesteps Shopify's closed business profile.
3. **Join the standards thread now.** #502, #738, #845, #929 are active this week; the people writing them (Intuit, Google London, Shopware, I Want That, Stabile, Facet) are reachable in public. Non-price terms are explicitly unowned.
4. **Personal Agent Protocol v0.1** (due later in October) starts with website discovery and allows routing to "the company's agent". Read it on release for a sanctioned way to advertise a store-side negotiating agent to Muse.
5. **Copy Google's token design** for the offer token: signed, short expiry, merchant id, offer/variant id, price or term, reject on any mismatch.
6. **One-shot quotes, not chat.** Flux, UCP #929 and the first-proposal-bias result all point to accept/decline/quote in a single response with tight rate limits.

## 7. Could not verify

- Flux MCP tool names and schemas (endpoint requires Flux ID sign-in; I did not create an account). The "Negotiate with Flux" GPT/app listing inside ChatGPT (link on the site has no href in static HTML). Flux traction numbers (counters render client-side).
- How Nibble applies a negotiated price on Shopify (help centre is login-walled; demo store password-protected). WooCommerce mechanism is verified from source code.
- Whether the Stabile test order's code was typed by the agent or by the human at checkout.
- Whether I Want That's "Expanded UCP support" is available on Shopify (table ticks are images), and the claim "Shopify blocked it" (founder statement only).
- Whether a third-party app can write the custom FAQ entries that Shopify Knowledge Base serves to agents.
- Whether StoreKnows' "storefront tools" are WebMCP registrations (wording suggests it; not inspected on a live store).
- Stripe "orders tagged with the originating agent" (not in the two Stripe docs pages read).
- Google Direct Offers billing model and whether third parties can create offers programmatically.
- Topsort Sponsored Prompts details (press releases returned 403).
- Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowe's, B&H, BBQGuys price-match wording (403/geo); the Target competitor list; the GERAD paper's "100% of top-20" figure (search summary only).
- PriceWaiter's exact end date and reason; Nibble's funding and customer count (Fortune via search summary).
- Whether UCP catalog responses on Shopify carry GTIN/barcode (not in the saved docs).
- Firmly, Rye, Skyfire, Paid, Nekuda product details beyond search summaries.
- UCP #264 / #287 (eligibility attestation) contents; UCP #937 Hosted Business Directory details; A2CN spec (only the Shopware discovery document was read).

## 8. Corrections and additions to the brief

1. Brief item 5 ("UCP has NO offer, counter-offer or price-negotiation message"): correct for the released spec, but there are now open proposals that add exactly these: #738/#773 State-bound Offer extension (merchant-proposed cart change, carried as Actions, `apply_offer`), #929/#930 Quote extension (`quote.proposal.subtotal` from the buyer; Business answers quoted/accepted/declined; filed 11 Oct 2026 by a Google engineer), #845 accepted-terms handoff, discussion #502. None is merged.
2. Brief item 6 (extensions need both profiles; Shopify generates the store's profile): confirmed again on fluxdemo.myshopify.com (ten capability keys, all `dev.ucp.*`/`dev.shopify.*`, including `dev.ucp.shopping.permalink` and `dev.ucp.common.identity_linking`), by Stabile on four stores, and by a founder who says Shopify blocked his namespaced capability. Addition: vendors publish their own UCP profile on their own domain instead (Flux), and UCP #384 would add a Provider slot on the platform side.
3. Brief item 11 can be upgraded from "reported by press": the Personal Agent Protocol post and Google's Direct Offers pages are now read at the primary source (2.4, 2.6). Direct Offers is beyond "pilot in AI Mode": per Google's GML 2026 page it now appears in the AI Mode answer, supports Gemini-constructed bundles within merchant guardrails, has "native checkout integration for UCP merchants", and is creatable by AI Max and PMax advertisers in the Google Ads UI. Stripe's promotion feed is confirmed; the order-tagging claim is not.
4. Idea A is not hypothetical: at least four Shopify apps and Google's automated discounts already deliver an agent- or ad-originated private price as a generated discount code. What is unproven is the multi-effect Discount Function and binding a code to one buyer.
5. Idea B(v) exists in production (Flux and Stabile ChatGPT apps, MCP connectors), with cross-store discovery at Flux.
6. Idea E has live examples outside Shopify (Shopware demo store publishes `com.shopware.quote` and `com.a2cn.negotiation-mandate`).
7. Add to the list of agent-to-store inputs worth watching: ACP's `intent_trace` (reason code + competitor price) and proposed `suggested_price {amount, source, observed_at}`; UCP's proposed `quote.proposal`.
8. For competitor-link verification on Shopify-hosted competitors: public `/products.json` has price/availability/SKU per variant but no GTIN, JSON-LD may be absent, and UCP `lookup_catalog` takes only Shopify GIDs. Plan on SKU/title/option matching plus an allow-list, not GTIN.

# G1 - Shopify: who controls the missing pieces (people, roles, channels, venues)

Research date: 13 Oct 2026. Every role below was confirmed from a page fetched today unless it says "unverified". Nobody was contacted. Nothing was posted, starred, followed or signed up for. All requests were read-only GETs of public pages (GitHub reads went through the `gh` CLI, GET only).

Labels: [P] = primary source read today (the organisation's own page, the person's own profile or post, a maintainer file, official minutes). [S] = press or other secondary source. [I] = my inference.

Raw copies of what I fetched: `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/docs/g1/` (subfolders `forum/`, `x/`, `ucp-minutes/`).

---

## 0. Short answer

1. The one person who owns the exact Shopify piece and openly invites contact is **Gil Greenberg** (Staff Product Manager, agentic commerce; UCP Shopping Tech Council member since 15 Sep 2026). He gave the DotDev 2026 talk "How Shopify Functions help you succeed in agentic checkouts", he announced checkout WebMCP, his site says "Reach out on social media ... (I respond best on Twitter)", and in the developer forum he wrote "I'd love to hear about any use cases you're blocked on, what we're missing". He is the best first target, ahead of Tobi Lutke.
2. The protocol piece (an offer message in UCP) is already moving without us: the Shopping Tech Council discussed "Structured Cart Modifications and State-Bound Offers" on 2 Oct 2026 (PR #773, issue #738, milestone 2026-12-08, assignee Greg Smith of Google). **Ilya Grigorik** (Shopify; Governance Council) was the sceptic in the room: he "probed whether platforms and agent builders would trust or utilize merchant-recommended products". The useful move is a factual comment on #738, not a cold DM.
3. Shopify has said in public, through staff on its developer forum, that apps cannot extend the store's agent surface today and that this is a known gap: "Extending UCP to expose these kinds of fulfilment details is a known gap and is on our radar. At this time, developers can't add to or adjust a merchant's /.well-known/ucp endpoint." (Wes, Shopify Staff, 21 Aug 2026). A thread that asks precisely OfferAd's question ("Managing Offers from Agents", 13 Apr 2026) has had no reply in six months.
4. Shopify already has a precedent for "apps contribute to Shopify's agent": **Sidekick App Extensions** (merchant side, GA in the Spring '26 Edition, "Any developer in Shopify's ecosystem can now build in Sidekick"). The ask to Shopify can be framed as "the same model for the buyer-facing agent surface".
5. Tobi Lutke is confirmed as CEO and is very unlikely to read a cold note; his last relevant public statement is the 21 Sep 2026 post about Muse and Shop Pay. A short public reply or quote-post that names a concrete gap is the only realistic way to reach him, and it should come after the Gil/forum/UCP routes have something to point to.

## 2. What Shopify has said in public about apps extending the agent surface, and about offers or negotiation

1. [P] Apps cannot extend the UCP profile; known gap. Wes, Shopify Staff, 21 Aug 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/36329 : "Extending UCP to expose these kinds of fulfilment details is a known gap and is on our radar. At this time, developers can't add to or adjust a merchant's /.well-known/ucp endpoint."
2. [P] No extension point in the UCP tools. Kyle Giesbrecht, Shopify Staff, 28 Jul 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/36233 : "the UCP catalog and checkout tools use a fixed, standardized schema so there's no extension point for custom product fields or custom checkout logic through the MCP tools themselves. UCP is built for interoperability, so any agent can shop any merchant's store using the same protocol." On 19 Aug 2026 he added: "the core constraint hasn't changed" and "I'll pass this along as a feature suggestion."
3. [P] The offers question is unanswered. Thread "Managing Offers from Agents", Chris Daly, 13 Apr 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/33264 : "we are trying to ascertain if we can surface to the agent that the shop accepts offers from consumers/agents ... It could include a counter offer, so if an Agent offers $75 for a $99 offer the shop could counter offer IRT with $80 and $5 flat shipping to try an secure the order. Is there a way to surface that for the shop?" Zero replies as of 13 Oct 2026.
4. [P] agents.md is the documented, merchant-editable discovery file. Liam Griffin, 20 May 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/34049 : "Shopify now uses /agents.md as the primary storefront discovery file for agentic and AI experiences ... To customize the discovery file itself, create or update templates/agents.md.liquid in your theme." Donal, 29 Jun 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/35418 : "agents.md.liquid renders in the same restricted context as robots.txt.liquid, and shop.metafields isn't hydrated there." So an app cannot feed that file through shop metafields today; only a theme edit can.
5. [P] Merchant metafields do not reach agents through the catalog tools. Paige, 8 Sep 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/37487 : "Shopify doesn't populate the product metadata field in Storefront Catalog MCP responses. Product metafields aren't mapped into it".
6. [P] Agent checkout completion is by grant only. Alan, 2 Sep 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/36590 : "Direct complete_checkout is a granted on a case by case basis and there isn't a public application or waitlist for self-serve platforms at the moment."
7. [P] No public partnership intake for agentic builders. Alan, 1 Jul 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/35628 : "I'm not aware of a separate public intake form or Community-based process for business development / strategic partnership discussions around AI commerce or storefront-builder tools at the moment. I'd agree that the best next step is to get in touch with Partner Support while logged in to your Partner account ... they can route internally if there's an applicable path."
8. [P] Functions are Shopify's stated answer for app logic in agentic checkout. Gil, 9 Jul 2026, https://community.shopify.dev/t/35930 : "validation functions work across every checkout surface, including agentic checkouts"; "migrate that logic to the discount Function API, which now supports rejecting discount codes with a custom message."
9. [P] Precedent: apps do extend Shopify's merchant agent. Newsroom, 17 Jun 2026, https://www.shopify.com/news/spring-26-edition-dev : "Now, any developer in Shopify's ecosystem can build a Sidekick App Extension." Docs, https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/sidekick : "Sidekick currently supports integrations with up to 20 apps for each user on a store."
10. [P] Shopify's own blog acknowledges agent-to-agent discount requests as an emerging model. https://www.shopify.com/blog/agentic-commerce (by Lauren Scherr, updated 25 Sep 2026): "In an emerging agent-to-agent model, which is still largely in development, a shopper's AI agent might request a discount from a retailer's agent without either party manually intervening." This is editorial content, not a product commitment.
11. [P] Shopify's own monetisation of agent surfaces: "Promoted placements will give developers and partners a future path to earn revenue when their Catalog-powered experiences drive sales" and "Shop Campaigns ... now includes ChatGPT" (newsroom, 17 Jun 2026). [I] Shopify may see seller offers to agents as its own territory.
12. [P] In the UCP council Shopify's representative questioned the offer idea but agreed there is demand (minutes 2 Oct 2026, quoted in 1.2).
13. I found no Shopify statement that says apps will be able to register a tool, add an agents.md section, or receive `context.intent` in a Function, and no statement that says they will not.

Not found: an upcoming Shopify or UCP developer event in San Francisco. The UCP governance file mentions "a shared Google group with a mailing list" for public discussion, but I found no link to it.

## 6. Method notes

- X: profile pages do not load without login. Single posts were verified through the public embed endpoint `cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result?id=<id>`, and profile bios through `syndication.twitter.com/srv/timeline-profile/screen-name/<handle>`. The second endpoint returns an unordered sample of old posts, so it cannot be used to find a person's newest post, and it rate-limits quickly.
- Shopify developer forum: Discourse JSON (`/t/<id>.json`, `/c/agentic/30.json`, `/u/<name>.json`, `/search.json`) is public and read-only. Some requests with `?print=true` returned 422; plain requests with a pause worked.
- GitHub: the unauthenticated API quota on this machine was used up, so reads went through `gh api -X GET` (read-only).
- help.shopify.com returned 403 to curl.

# G2: Meta, Sierra and Stripe: who controls the missing pieces, and how to reach them

Research date: 13 Oct 2026. Every page cited below was fetched on that day unless marked otherwise. Raw copies are in `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/docs/g2/`. Nobody was contacted. Nothing was posted, signed up for or submitted.

Labels: **[P]** primary (the organisation's own page, the person's own post or profile, a maintainer file). **[S]** secondary (press or a conference bio). **[snippet]** seen only as a search-result summary, page not read. **[inferred]** my reading.

How X posts were read: through X's public embed endpoint (`cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result`), which returns the author, date and the first 280 characters. Long posts are cut at that length; I quote only what was returned.

---

## 1. Short answers to the questions in the task

1. **Alexandr Wang's current title.** "Chief AI Officer, Meta Superintelligence Labs", as printed on 12 Oct 2026 in the description of an interview he gave with Mark Zuckerberg. Not taken from a Meta page: Meta's executive pages returned HTTP 400 and the investor leadership page returned 403.
2. **Does Muse sit in his organisation?** Muse is a Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) product, and Wang's title is Chief AI Officer of MSL. Meta's own Muse safety post is signed "Software Engineer & VP, Meta Superintelligence Labs". Zuckerberg on 12 Oct 2026 described the product work as done by "the people on Nat's team". The formal reporting line from Nat Friedman to Wang is not confirmed by anything dated 2026; the only source is a 2025 press report repeated on Wikipedia.
3. **Nat Friedman.** Head of product at MSL per TechCrunch (22 Sep 2026); his own X posts and Zuckerberg's remarks are consistent with that. He is the person who runs the Muse product team.
4. **Muse Connector Platform lead and developer relations.** No named person found. The platform was announced by Zuckerberg himself. The guidelines say "we cannot respond to individual messages or emails about status". The only route is the submission portal behind a login.
5. **Meta on UCP.** James Andersen (UCP Shopping Tech Council; roster file changed 12 Oct 2026).
6. **Meta on ACP.** Lee Hwa (`lhwa`) holds Meta's seat on the ACP Technical Steering Committee. Vignesh Sreedhar (`vig-star`, San Francisco) wrote the most recently merged ACP change.
7. **Meta on the Personal Agent Protocol.** David Singleton made Meta's announcement on X and gave Meta's press interview.
8. **Who edits the PAP draft.** Not named anywhere on personalagentprotocol.org. The site says "The spec's authors" and "The people working on the draft". Feedback goes to one Sierra mailbox. There is no public repository, issue tracker or working-group sign-up.
9. **How an outsider comments on PAP.** Two documented ways, both ending in an email to `[EMAIL REDACTED]` (section 4.1).
10. **Stripe.** Kevin Miller (executive, payments), Jeff Weinstein (product lead, agentic commerce, title last printed Sep 2025), Steve Kaliski (engineering lead), Prasad Wangikar (Stripe's ACP seat and the person who runs ACP's admin), Jake Sinsheimer (go-to-market).
11. **How to propose an ACP change.** A GitHub issue tagged `SEP` and `proposal`, a sponsor from the steering committee, a seven-business-day review, a simple-majority vote (section 4.2). The repository has not merged anything since 18 Jul 2026.
12. **Is "Reconsideration Offers" already proposed?** No. A search of the ACP repository for "reconsideration" returns one item, the original Intent Traces pull request. The slot is open.

---

## 2. What each organisation has said in public that bears on the idea

### Meta

- Wang, 12 Oct 2026 [P, interview transcript]: "I think Muse is one of the first products where you’re actually people are fully delegating purchases to the agents." https://cheekypint.substack.com/p/muse-wonder-zuckerberg-and-wangs
- Wang, same interview: "I think agentic commerce demand will grow as a portion of the pie." and "do they want to participate in that slice or that portion of the economy over time?"
- Zuckerberg, same interview: "over time there are lots of different ways to effectively take a small cut of what you are saving or making for people, and that will end up being a very large revenue stream."
- Zuckerberg, same interview, on why Muse can buy anywhere: "now you can ask your muse to buy anything, more or less. And it’ll just figure it out with computer use, right? And so it’s like the ultimate backwards compatibility layer."
- Wang to CNBC, 8 Sep 2026 [S]: "We think the commerce business model is potentially really interesting for this product because of how much it enables people to to actually find the things that they are excited about and ultimately fulfill a lot of those purchases," and CNBC's paraphrase: "The company is exploring potential monetary initiatives, such as taking a cut of AI agent-related shopping transactions, but hasn't settled on any concrete plan". https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/08/meta-personal-ai-agents-public-reckoning-privacy-safety.html
- Meta newsroom, 8 Sep 2026 (updated 30 Sep) [P]: Muse "can open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate on their behalf" and "When it comes time to pay, Muse can checkout with Link built by Stripe". "Shop Pay is coming soon as another way to pay". https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/
- Muse connector guidelines [P, undated, fetched today], the rules an offer connector would be judged by. https://muse.ai/platform/docs
  - 1.2: "Muse can already browse websites. Your connector should improve on what’s possible in the browser experience through better information, account access, more reliable actions, or fewer steps." and "A wrapper around public pages or a list of links alone is not enough."
  - 1.1: "Sending the user to finish the entire checkout does not meet the completion requirement."
  - 3.2: "Do not use tool descriptions or responses to instruct Muse to ignore its rules, steer away from competitors, access unrelated data, force recommendations, conceal commercial interests, or take unrequested actions."
  - 4.3: "Label advertising, sponsored results, and commercial relationships that influence recommendations. Do not fabricate reviews, urgency, discounts, or successful outcomes."
  - 5.2: "Provide the business information and supporting evidence requested to verify your organization and your authority to submit the connector."
  - 5.7: "Check the portal for your connector’s review status. Due to submission volume, we cannot respond to individual messages or emails about status."
  - 6: "We review submissions in three stages. Meeting these guidelines does not guarantee approval."
  - 7.1: "Approved connectors are discoverable by the Muse agent and in Settings > Connectors."
- Muse platform page [P]: "We'll review your connector for functional, security, and legal requirements, and complete end to end testing." and "we've partnered with Stripe to make accepting payments easy with Link." https://muse.ai/platform
- Meta newsroom, 29 Sep 2026 (updated 8 Oct) [P]: "Interested partners can apply at muse.ai/platform. Muse also supports custom connectors so you can plug in services we don’t support yet". https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/
- [inferred] Rule 4.3 allows sponsored results if labelled, and forbids fabricated discounts. An offer connector that returns real, checkout-enforced offers and labels them as seller offers fits the wording. Rule 3.2 (no steering away from competitors) means the competing-offer link must be something the buyer's agent chooses to pass, never something the tool asks Muse to do. Rule 1.1 is the hard one for a Shopify app: a connector that ends in a cart link may be judged incomplete.

### Sierra and the Personal Agent Protocol (PAP, "Poppy")

- Draft 0.1, "Updated Oct 12, 2026" on every docs page. https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/introduction
- The draft has no offer, discount, promotion or negotiation message. Word counts in the spec and the Operations extension: "discount" 0, "negotiat" 0, "promotion" 0; "offer" appears only in the ordinary sense (a company "offers" an API).
- The closest primitive is the Operations extension [P]: "The operations extension lets a Company ask the Personal Agent to confirm an action before the Company performs it". "Approval covers the exact terms. The User approves one revision of the terms, and the Company performs only what that revision describes." Each operation carries `summary`, `terms`, `revision`, `expires_at`. "Terms can change before confirmation, for example when the User asks for a different size. The Company then issues a new revision of the same operation". https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/extensions/operations
- Anyone can define an extension without permission [P]: "Extensions defined on this site have plain names, such as operations. Anyone can define their own, named with a domain they control, such as example.com/gift-wrap." It only works if the personal agent also lists it: "A personal agent lists the extensions it supports in extensions in its client metadata document". https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/extensions
- What the authors ask for [P]: "Broadly useful extensions. Things many implementations need, such as payments, that could be built as extensions." Open topics listed: payments, push notifications, attachments. Offers are not listed. https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/path-to-1
- Sierra, 9 Oct 2026 [P]: "Protocols such as Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) focus on shopping, from finding products to checking out and managing orders. Personal Agent Protocol is complementary". "Over the next month we will host design workshops and publish a reference implementation to help developers get started." https://sierra.ai/blog/poppy
- Shopify is listed as a technology-provider design partner, and Meta, OpenAI and Instinct as personal-agent design partners. Same page.
- [inferred] A seller offer fits PAP as "an operation the Company proposes with better terms than the agent asked for", or as a named extension (for example `offerad.<domain>/offers`). Either needs Muse to list the extension, which is Meta's decision, not Sierra's.

### Stripe and ACP

- Kevin Miller, Stripe Sessions keynote, 29 Apr 2026 [P]: "Payments is about to meet a new kind of buyer: agents." and "We think of this as a spectrum where, at one end, agents help customers discover, but the human still chooses and buys. In the middle, the human chooses and the agent checks out. And at the far end, the agent discovers and buys." Also: "today I’m pleased to announce that Shopify will become the preferred catalog provider for retailers that want to integrate with the Agentic Commerce Suite." https://stripe.com/sessions/2026/opening-remarks-and-product
- Kevin Miller in Sierra's post, 6 Oct 2026 [P for the quote]: "A customer relationship doesn’t start or end at checkout. When customers send an agent, they expect the same service they’d get themselves. We’re contributing to the Personal Agent Protocol to give businesses a standard way to recognize their customers’ agents, efficiently interact with them, and shape their customer relationships." https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol
- John Collison, 12 Oct 2026 [P, transcript]: "it’s very interesting to look at the agentic commerce stats at Stripe because we started developing all this stuff and we had a whole bunch of announcements at Sessions back in May, uh, and then it only as of September basically started going vertical." (He says May; Stripe's newsroom dates Sessions 29 Apr 2026.)
- ACP Intent Traces RFC, on `main`, "Status: Proposal" [P]: "This specification lays the groundwork for merchants to transition from probabilistic retargeting (guessing) to deterministic negotiation (bidding)." and "Future extensibility: A subsequent RFC MAY define **Reconsideration Offers** keyed to specific reason codes." https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol/blob/main/rfcs/rfc.intent_traces.md
- The Intent Traces pull request (#54, by `0xtotaylor`, opened 17 Dec 2025, closed 11 Jan 2026) states the motive in the seller's terms: "A merchant receiving `reason_code: shipping_cost` can programmatically respond with a free shipping offer rather than guessing."
- ACP Suggested Pricing (Lee Hwa, Meta; pull request #201, merged 22 May 2026) [P]: "the agent provides the seller with the information needed to make an informed decision about whether to honor the price the buyer saw."
- ACP governance rule that limits how a proposal may be worded [P]: not permitted: "Using ACP channels or governance forums for product marketing or self-promotion." and "Making direct comparisons between competing products or services within ACP discussions." https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol/blob/main/docs/governance.md
- [inferred] ACP is the one place where the text of the standard already names the missing message. A "Reconsideration Offers" proposal continues the maintainers' own sentence. The weakness found by sibling research still holds: ChatGPT sends Shopify buyers to the merchant's checkout, so ACP traffic to Shopify stores is thin.
