## 4. Official venues and the exact steps

### 4.1 Personal Agent Protocol: commenting on the draft
Source: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/path-to-1 ("Draft 0.1, Updated Oct 12, 2026") and the review kit served at `https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/review-kit.json`.

- Who may comment: "Feedback is welcome from anyone, whether or not you're a partner."
- What they want: "Privacy and security", "Gaps in the spec", "Simplification", "Broadly useful extensions. Things many implementations need, such as payments, that could be built as extensions."
- Way 1: "Use the site's inline comments. You can comment on any text on this site, then export your comments to share them. Enable site commenting, then select text to comment on it. To export, use the … button next to Comments."
- Way 2: "Review with an agent. If you'd like an agent to review the docs and write feedback, download the agent kit. It contains all the docs and an AGENTS.md that tells the agent how to write feedback in a form we can easily use."
- Where it goes: "Email either kind of feedback to [EMAIL REDACTED]."
- Licence on what is sent: "you grant all other members and users of the protocol a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to use, modify, and commercialize that feedback for any purpose, without compensation or other obligation to you." https://personalagentprotocol.org/license/contributions
- Format the authors ask for (from AGENTS.md in the kit): one Markdown file titled "Review of the Personal Agent Protocol docs (2026-10-12)", a two or three sentence summary, then points grouped by section, each labelled **Gap**, **Ambiguous**, **Contradiction**, **Risk**, **Wording** or **Question**, with headings such as "Specification › 3.1 Fields (`spec#fields`)". "For each point, say what's wrong and why it matters, and suggest a fix when you have one." "Skip praise and nitpicks unless asked."
- The sections an offers point belongs under: `extensions-operations#operations`, `extensions-operations#revisions`, `extensions-operations#proposing`, `spec#extensions`, and "General".
- The inline comment tool stores comments in the browser and exports them; nothing is public. There is no public thread to read or join.

### 4.2 Personal Agent Protocol: joining as a design partner
Same page: "We're welcoming new partners. To join, email [EMAIL REDACTED] with: Which group you fall into: personal agent, company, or technology provider. A technical contact, for the implementation work. A partnership contact, for everything else."
- A Shopify app that serves merchants would be a "technology provider".
- Every listed partner is a large company. Nothing says individuals are excluded and nothing says they are admitted.
- "Working group": the site does not use the term. The only sources for it are a Decagon X post quoted by a third-party blog [S]. There is no charter, mailing list or meeting schedule.
- Design workshops: announced twice ("host design workshops with interested parties", 6 Oct; "Over the next month we will host design workshops", 9 Oct). No date, place or sign-up page found.

### 4.3 ACP: proposing "Reconsideration Offers"
Sources: `docs/governance.md`, `docs/sep-guidelines.md`, `docs/operating-model.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` in https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol

1. Check it needs the formal route. It does: "Adding, modifying, or removing features in the specification (e.g., new API endpoints, messages, or data structures)" is a Major Change, and Major Changes "must follow the SEP process".
2. Optional first step: "Community members can discuss ideas in `#general` on Discord before filing." Also: "Start with a GitHub Discussion or Issue before creating a SEP".
3. File it: "You, the SEP author, create a well-formatted GitHub Issue with the `SEP` and `proposal` tags. The SEP number is the same as the GitHub Issue number".
4. Required parts: Preamble, Abstract ("~200 word"), Motivation ("SEP submissions without sufficient motivation may be rejected outright"), Specification ("A PR with the changes to the specification should be provided"), Rationale, Backward Compatibility, Reference Implementation, Security Implications.
5. Get a sponsor: "Every SEP must be sponsored by a TSC member to proceed." The seats today: OpenAI (`aravindrao-openai`), Stripe (`prasad-stripe`), Meta (`lhwa`). "Sponsorship discussion happens in `#technical-steering-committee`", which is members-only.
6. Review: "a mandatory 7-business-day public review window", which "must span across at least one instance of the weekly TSC meeting" (Thursday, 30 minutes, "time TBD").
7. Vote: "SEPs are adopted or rejected by a simple majority vote (50%+1) of the TSC." With three seats that is two votes. OpenAI and Stripe each hold a veto over SEPs, to block only.
8. Acceptance criteria: "A prototype implementation demonstrating the proposal", "Clear benefit to the ACP ecosystem", "Community support and consensus".
9. Time limit: "If the SEP has not found a sponsor within three months, Founding Maintainers may close the SEP as `dormant`."
10. The pull request needs: OpenAPI and JSON Schema under `spec/unreleased/`, examples in `examples/`, a file in `changelog/unreleased/`, the `sep-proposal.md` template, and a signed Individual CLA (the bot asks on the first pull request; "This takes less than 1 minute").
11. Tone rule: no "product marketing or self-promotion" and no "direct comparisons between competing products" in ACP channels. The proposal must not mention the app.

State of the repository, read today:
- Last commit on `main`: 18 Jul 2026. `pushed_at` is the same date. Nothing merged in almost three months.
- 144 open issues and pull requests. The 40 most recently updated carry no labels and no assignee, including SEPs filed in July, August and September.
- The two process documents disagree: `sep-guidelines.md` says sponsorship by "a Founding Maintainer or Maintainer (future tier)" and review "by the ACP Founding Maintainers team on a bi-weekly basis"; `governance.md` says a TSC sponsor and a weekly TSC vote. An open pull request from 16 Sep 2026 (#309, "Fix SEP sponsor/approval language in docs to match governance.md") is unmerged.
- Discussion #209 "ACP pattern for custom quoting before checkout creation?" (1 Apr 2026) has three comments, none from a maintainer account.
- Discussion #304 is a contributor asking in public for a sponsor for SEP #303; the same could be done.
- Discord invite printed in the operating model: https://discord.gg/53k84htnJ (not opened; joining needs an account).
- [inferred] The process is real and the hook is in the text, but the committee looks slow or quiet. A proposal filed cold may sit. Naming a sponsor first (Lee Hwa or Prasad Wangikar) is the step that decides the outcome.

### 4.4 Muse Connector Platform
Sources: https://muse.ai/platform and https://muse.ai/platform/docs . The terms page (https://muse.ai/platform/terms) returned HTTP 400.

1. Log in at muse.ai (the "Submit a connector" button leads to a login). Not done.
2. Submit: connector overview (5.1), business verification and terms (5.2), data processing questionnaire (5.3), endpoint, authentication and tool documentation for the API or MCP server (5.4), a test account and demo (5.5).
3. Review in three stages: risk assessment (6.1), tool review (6.2), end-to-end QA (6.3).
4. If approved: "discoverable by the Muse agent and in Settings > Connectors". Featuring "is a separate editorial decision".
5. No human contact: "we cannot respond to individual messages or emails about status." The one address on the page, [EMAIL REDACTED], is for security incidents only.
6. Business verification asks for "your organization and your authority to submit the connector", which may need a registered business.

### 4.5 Muse custom connectors
Meta, 29 Sep 2026: "Muse also supports custom connectors so you can plug in services we don’t support yet". The sibling notes quote Meta's help page: "Meta doesn't review custom connectors or how they use your information, so grant access with caution" (https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/1687253048996149/, saved copy from this morning, not re-fetched by me). A user can ask their own Muse to connect to an offer endpoint with no Meta approval. Useful for a demo and for early users; it is not distribution.

### 4.6 UCP, for the Meta and Stripe members
The roster is at https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md . James Andersen (Meta) and Prasad Wangikar (Stripe) sit on the Shopping Tech Council that reviews the open offer and quote proposals. The route is a comment on those open issues. The governance steps are covered by the sibling notes on UCP.

### 4.7 Not found
No Meta or Stripe office hours, no Muse developer-relations contact, no dated San Francisco event in this scope. Sierra Summit took place in San Francisco ("At Sierra Summit in San Francisco", Sierra's recap) on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 and has passed. The promised PAP design workshops are the only upcoming in-person route, and they have no public date.

## 5. Honest read on who to write to

1. **Highest value for effort:** a PAP review sent in the format the authors ask for, making one point: the draft has no way for a company to put a better or different offer in front of a personal agent, and the Operations extension is two fields away from carrying one. This reaches the people who edit the draft, whoever they are, while the draft is ten days old and they are asking for "broadly useful extensions".
2. **Second:** an ACP proposal for Reconsideration Offers, with Lee Hwa or Prasad Wangikar asked in advance. The maintainers' own text names it. Risk: a quiet committee and thin Shopify traffic.
3. **Third:** David Singleton, one question about whether Muse will honour a merchant-declared extension. He is the one senior Meta person who is both named on PAP and plausibly reachable.
4. **Wang and Friedman:** the owner asked for them, and the note can truthfully refer to Wang's 12 Oct remark about delegated purchases. Expect no reply. A public post with a working demo that tags them is more likely to be seen than a direct message.
5. **Tobi Lutke** is outside this file's scope and belongs to the Shopify file.

# G3: people and venues at OpenAI, xAI, Perplexity, Anthropic, Microsoft, Decagon and Instinct

Research date: 13 Oct 2026. Scope: agent makers other than Meta and Google. Nobody was contacted; nothing was posted, starred, followed or submitted; no account was created. All fetches were read-only GETs of public pages. GitHub data was read through the public REST API.

Raw copies of every page quoted below are in `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/docs/g3/` (file names are given per item).

Labels: **[P]** primary (the organisation's own page, the person's own profile or post, a maintainer file). **[S]** secondary (press, interviewer's page, third-party summary). **[snippet]** seen only as a search-result snippet, page itself not fetched. **[I]** my inference.

---

## 0. Short version

1. The person who owns the exact piece at OpenAI is not an executive. For the protocol it is **Aravind Rao** (OpenAI's seat on the ACP steering committee and author of the Promotions API proposal), reachable on a public GitHub issue. For the product it is **Alexander Embiricos** (leads Dots), who speaks in San Francisco on 15 Oct 2026 at TechCrunch Disrupt. For the directory rules the honest route is the plugin portal plus **Romain Huet** (Head of Developer Experience) as the person who can point to the right reviewer.
2. **Holly Li**: the only description I could confirm is "OpenAI product team member" who ran the Dots stage demo. No formal title found. She is not a verified owner of anything and should not be a target.
3. **Roman Ugarte**: confirmed as the person who "helped incubate and build Grok Bot" at SpaceXAI (8 Sep 2026). Search snippets say he "now leads product for Grok Bot" and his X bio reads "building @Bot at @SpaceXAI". No exact title on a page I could fetch.
4. Grok Bot's connector catalog is the **Cursor Marketplace**, not an xAI-run directory. It is curated, manually reviewed, open-source only, and takes applications at a public form. xAI publishes no rule about offers or ads in connectors.
5. Perplexity takes connector proposals only from companies, through a form and a published team address. The named business owner is **Dmitry Shevelenko** (Chief Business Officer).
6. Microsoft's named Copilot Checkout lead is **Nayna Sheth**, Head of Product for Agentic Payments. Microsoft's voice in UCP is **Patrick Jordan**.
7. PACT (Decagon with Instinct) is the most open door in this scope: a nine-day-old repo with a public issue tracker and one committer, **Harry Gao**. A commerce-related issue (#59) is already open. The maintainers have not answered any issue yet.
8. Every reviewed directory in this scope either bans ad vehicles in words (OpenAI, Anthropic) or is curated by hand (Cursor, Perplexity). The policy question "is a seller's concrete, checkout-valid offer an advertisement?" is the single most useful thing to ask, and nobody has answered it in public.

- Michelle Fradin (named in 2025 coverage as leading ChatGPT commerce) has no 2026 source I could find. **Unverified; do not use.**
- Fidji Simo stepped down from the full-time CEO of Applications role: "Fidji Simo, OpenAI's No. 2 executive, is stepping down from her full-time role" and "Weil has since left the company, too." (TechCrunch, 9 Jul 2026, https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/09/fidji-simo-steps-down-from-openais-no-2-role/ , `tc-simo.html`). Neither Simo nor Kevin Weil should be addressed as the owner of ChatGPT product.
- Ads (adjacent, sales side) **[S]**: "David Dugan, the former Meta agency executive who leads OpenAI's global ads solutions team"; his LinkedIn profile "lists the role of VP, Head of Global Ads Solutions from March 2026". His own LinkedIn post as quoted by the same article: "Excited to announce that our ChatGPT ads business has surpassed a $1B annualized run rate, less than 200 days since launch". PPC Land, about 21 Sep 2026 (article undated in markup; it says the post was "three weeks old" and the announcement was 31 Aug 2026). https://ppc.land/openais-david-dugan-says-chatgpt-ads-passed-a-1bn-run-rate/ (`ppcland-dugan.html`). He sells the incumbent ad format; he is not a route for a builder. Not proposed as a target.

### 1.7 OpenAI: public routes for a developer, and the policy text

All **[P]**, fetched 13 Oct 2026.

- Plugin submission portal: https://platform.openai.com/plugins . "Open Plugins and select **Upload new or existing plugin**." "Complete individual or business verification in organization settings to publish under your name or a company name." (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission.md , `openai-plugin-submission.md`). An individual can publish under his own name: "If you want to publish under your own name, complete **individual verification**." (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/app-review.md)
- Appeal: "If the review team rejects your submission, check the rejection email for the reason. To appeal, reply to that email and explain why the decision should be reconsidered." And: "Please do not contact support to request expedited review, as these requests cannot be accommodated."
- No review needed for personal use: the directory has a "**Personal:** personal marketplace plugins, including **Created by me** and **Shared with me** sections" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins.md). Dots use them: "Your dot can use supported plugins installed and enabled for your account, with their connected accounts and existing permissions." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots.md)
- Developer forum: https://community.openai.com , category "ChatGPT Apps SDK" (549 topics), read from the public categories list (`openai-community-categories.json`).
- Merchant programme (feeds, promotions): "To apply for access, fill out this form here" pointing at https://chatgpt.com/merchants (commerce docs, https://developers.openai.com/commerce/llms-full.txt). That page returns 403 to automated fetches.
- ACP: public issue tracker and Discussions at https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol ; a SEP needs a TSC sponsor.
- Plugin guidelines (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/plugin-guidelines.md , `openai-plugin-guidelines.md`), the lines that bear on an offer connector:
  - "Plugins must not serve advertisements and must not exist primarily as an advertising vehicle. Every plugin must deliver clear, legitimate functionality that provides standalone value to users."
  - "**Unofficial connectors:** We cannot approve plugins that primarily function as unofficial connectors to third-party services, including pass-through intermediary software layers."
  - "**Subtitles and descriptions:** ... Do not advertise pricing, subscriptions, free trials, discounts, or promotions."
  - "Currently, plugins may conduct commerce only for physical goods."
  - "Plugins should use external checkout, directing users to complete purchases on your own domain."
  - "Plugins must not apply ChatGPT-specific fees, surcharges, or other pricing that penalizes users for accessing a service through ChatGPT. Temporary discounts and promotional offers on other platforms are permitted."
  - "Avoid misleading, overly promotional, or comparative language (for example, `pick_me`, `best`, `official`)." (tool names)
  - "Plugins that demonstrate strong real-world utility and high user satisfaction may be eligible for enhanced distribution opportunities, such as directory placement or proactive suggestions."
- **[I]** Reading: a per-merchant plugin published by the merchant fits the text. A cross-store offer broker run by a third party collides with "unofficial connectors ... pass-through intermediary" and risks "advertising vehicle". The text does not say whether a seller's own concrete offer is an advertisement.

## 8. Public positions that touch offers or ads (exact text)

1. OpenAI plugin guidelines: "Plugins must not serve advertisements and must not exist primarily as an advertising vehicle."
2. OpenAI plugin guidelines: "We cannot approve plugins that primarily function as unofficial connectors to third-party services, including pass-through intermediary software layers."
3. OpenAI plugin guidelines: "Temporary discounts and promotional offers on other platforms are permitted."

# G4: Google, WebMCP and UCP governance: who controls the missing pieces

Fetched and checked on 13 Oct 2026. Nobody was contacted. Nothing was posted, starred, followed or signed up for. Only public pages and public GitHub API reads.

Raw copies of every page quoted here: `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/docs/g4/`

Labels used: **[P]** primary source read today (organisation's own page, the person's own profile or post, a maintainer file, a spec). **[S]** press or other secondary source. **[I]** my inference.

---

## 0. Short version

1. **UCP has an open door for exactly this idea, and it is being decided in the next eight weeks.** Two proposals cover "offer" semantics: the state-bound Offer extension (#738 with PR #773, by an outside author at Intuit) is on the `2026-12-08` milestone and assigned to Greg Smith (Google); the Quote extension (#929 with draft PR #930, filed 11 Oct 2026 by a Google engineer in London) adds a Buyer `proposal` and names "the smallest in-protocol opening that lets a consumer agent make an offer without leaving UCP". Neither has a field for a competing-offer link or a non-price priority. That is the gap OfferAd can speak to with a working implementation.
2. **The governance documents tell an individual builder what to do first: ship under your own namespace.** "Vendors should first create capabilities & extensions in vendor-specific namespace pattern (e.g. com.{vendor}.\*) for new use cases. Requests to add new capabilities and extensions should only be submitted when there is proven widespread adoption". A core "offer" message is a Tech Council majority vote, twice. A working group needs "3+ organizations" and can only be nominated by a Tech Council member.
3. **The council itself says outside contributors "hit a wall"** (minutes, 4 Sep 2026) and that "items without an active implementer behind them are a signal to deprioritize" (18 Sep 2026). So the realistic route is an implementer note on the existing proposals, not a new proposal and not a cold note to a vice president.
4. **WebMCP is run in the open by three editors (two Google, one Microsoft) in a W3C Community Group that anyone can join for free.** The most active triager is Dominic Farolino (Google Chrome). His stated rule for new ideas: "implement it outside the spec, gather experience, and then file focused issues". The group meets every two weeks and face to face at TPAC in Dublin on 27 Oct 2026.
5. **Most reachable person in this scope: Kasper Kulikowski** (Senior Developer Relations Engineer, Google). He writes on his own blog about a user's agent meeting a website-side "harness" that "represents the business", and he wrote "if you try them, please reach out".
6. **Google's Direct Offers has no publicly named product lead.** The only named owners are Vidhya Srinivasan (VP/GM Ads and Commerce) and, for advertiser questions, Ginny Marvin (Ads Product Liaison). Press reports (7 Oct 2026) say the new "Direct Offer" asset settles through single-use promo codes uploaded as a CSV, the same settlement mechanism OfferAd uses.
7. **Role-staleness catch:** Greg Smith joined the UCP Tech Council in April 2026 as "Greg Smith (Amazon)"; the maintainer file moved him to Google on 1 Aug 2026 and gave the Amazon seat to Jordan Williams. Victoria Duggan (Shopify) left the Shopping Tech Council on 15 Sep 2026, replaced by Gil Greenberg. The older note H1 section 7 still lists Duggan.

## 1. UCP governance: the exact process

### 1.1 Who decides

Source [P]: `GOVERNANCE.md`, https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md (repository last pushed 12 Oct 2026).

- Governing Council (GC): "Responsible for governance, overall health and adoption of the protocol." "Includes a total of 5 members." "Includes 1 permanent member from each founding organization (Google & Shopify) each having 1 vote (total 2 votes)." "Includes 3 elected members from any organization". "Google holds proxy vote for all open seats until Dec 2028 to facilitate rapid early stage growth & adoption of the protocol." "May choose to review and veto a DTC decision or recommendation." "Decisions are made with a majority vote."
- [I] Today the GC has three named members and two open seats, and Google holds the proxy vote for the open seats. So Google controls three of five GC votes.
- Shopping Tech Council: "Responsible for building and maintaining core specification for the Shopping domain." "Includes 16 members, 4 permanent members from each founding organization (Google & Shopify), each with 1 vote (total 8 votes)." "Includes 8 members from any organization, each with 1 vote (total 8 votes)." "Decisions are made with a majority vote." "Members are elected by the GC every 6 months".
- Maintainers: "All code changes require approval from at least one Maintainer."

Source [P]: `MAINTAINERS.md`, https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md (last commit 12 Oct 2026, "replace Harsh Mehta with Simon Farrow on Payments Tech Council (#80)").

Governance Council today: Amit Handa (Google), Ilya Grigorik (Shopify), Twum Djin (Stripe), Open, Open.

Shopping Tech Council today (17 rows): Amit Handa\* (Google), Anurag Sinha (Google), Daniel Wyckoff (Shopify), Drew Olson (Google), Gil Greenberg (Shopify), Greg Smith (Google), Ilya Grigorik (Shopify), Imran Hoosain (Etsy), James Andersen (Meta), Jing Li (Google), Jordan Williams (Amazon), Lee Richmond (Shopify), Maxime Najim (Target), Patrick Jordan (Microsoft), Prasad Wangikar (Stripe), Scot DeDeo (Salesforce), Uddhav Kambli (Wayfair). "\* Standing Governing Council (GC) member participating per GOVERNANCE.md rules."

Maintainer file history [P] (GitHub commit log for MAINTAINERS.md):
- 2026-07-31 "docs: replace Greg Smith with Jordan Williams in MAINTAINERS.md (#51)" (row `Greg Smith | Amazon` removed, `Jordan Williams | Amazon` added; commit author Amit Handa).
- 2026-08-01 "docs: update MAINTAINERS list to include Greg Smith and denote Governing Council members (#52)" (row `Greg Smith | Google` added).
- 2026-09-15 "docs(maintainers): replace Victoria Duggan with Gil Greenberg on Shopping Tech Council (#71)".
- ucp.dev announcement of 24 Apr 2026 still reads "Greg Smith (Amazon)" (https://ucp.dev/documentation/announcements/). It is historical, not current.

### 1.2 Route A: a vendor extension such as `com.offerad.offer` (no permission needed)

Source [P]: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

> "UCP is designed to be extensible while keeping the core protocol light. A core principle of UCP is to ensure that the set of extensions and capabilities defined in UCP have broad ecosystem support. Vendors should first create capabilities & extensions in vendor-specific namespace pattern (e.g. com.{vendor}.\*) for new use cases. Requests to add new capabilities and extensions should only be submitted when there is proven widespread adoption of vendor-specific capabilities and extensions."

> "New features should typically be attempted through the extensions framework first. If an extension achieves significant usage, it can be considered for adoption into the next minor version of the core."

Source [P]: https://ucp.dev/documentation/contributing/ (fetched as index.md today)

> "New capabilities or extensions for vendor-specific or emerging use cases should first be self-hosted under a vendor namespace (e.g., `com.{vendor}.*`; see Namespace Governance) and proposed for adoption into `dev.ucp.*` once there is broad multi-party ecosystem adoption."

Source [P]: UCP specification overview, https://ucp.dev/specification/overview/ (version 2026-08-25)

> "The `dev.ucp.*` namespace is reserved for capabilities sanctioned by the UCP governing body. Vendors **MUST** use their own reverse-domain namespace for custom capabilities."

> "a declared `schema` URL's origin **MUST** match the namespace authority in its name."

> "This binding guarantees **provenance, not trust** ... Whether to negotiate, trust, or implement it is always the client's decision"

> A third-party extension "advertises exact extension versions in Business and Platform profiles and is negotiated by exact-version intersection like every capability."

What this means for OfferAd [I]:
- Nobody has to approve `com.offerad.offer`. The schema must be served over https from `offerad.com` (or a subdomain), because the name is bound to the domain. Whether the owner controls `offerad.com` was not checked.
- The extension only activates when BOTH profiles list it. Shopify generates the store's profile and no buyer agent lists it, so on Shopify today it is a published document, not a working channel. It still counts as the "self-hosted under a vendor namespace" first step that the governance text asks for.

### 1.3 Route B: a core change (an "offer" message in `dev.ucp.*`)

Source [P]: `CONTRIBUTING.md` (same URL)

> "Any significant change to the protocol requires a formal Enhancement Proposal and will require Tech Council (TC) approval."

Significant changes include "Core Schema Modifications", "Protocol Changes", "New API Endpoints: Introduction of entirely new capabilities or services", "Backwards Incompatibility".

Lifecycle, quoted:
> "**Proposal:** Anyone can submit; idea is proposed and debated."
> "**Provisional:** TC majority vote to accept; enters working draft iteration."
> "**Implemented:** TC majority vote to finalize; code complete and merged."

> "Every Enhancement Proposal must follow a standard template requiring sections for a Summary, Motivation, Detailed Design, Risks, a Test Plan, and Graduation Criteria."

The issue form itself [P] (https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/enhancement-proposal.yml; open it at https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/new?template=enhancement-proposal.yml): title prefix "[Proposal]: ", label `enhancement-proposal`, required fields Summary, Motivation, Goals, Detailed Design, Risks and Mitigations ("This is a mandatory section"), Test Plan ("A test plan is required for a proposal to be moved to the \"Provisional\" stage"), Graduation Criteria. Blank issues are disabled.

Step-by-step from ucp.dev [P]:
> "1. **Open the EP Issue First (`Proposal` Phase)**: Before writing full implementation code or opening a mergeable PR, submit the EP Issue. (Optional: You may open a Draft PR linked to the EP Issue ...)"
> "2. **Design Review & Provisional Approval**: Triagers label the EP Issue by functional domain (e.g., `area:shopping` ...) and route it to the relevant Domain Working Group (DWG) and Domain Tech Council (DTC). Once open design questions are resolved, the DTC votes on whether to accept the proposal as Provisional"
> "3. **Submit Implementation PRs (`Provisional` Phase)**"
> "4. **Iterate Toward Graduation** ... the DTC holds a final vote to mark the EP Implemented"

Maturity levels [P]: Working Draft ("Breaking changes expected") then Candidate ("Early adopter implementations, production pilots") then Stable; each step "TC majority vote to advance".

Escalation [P]: "L1: routine changes ... require approval from at least 2 Maintainers." "L2: ... Significant changes affecting core protocol architecture must follow the Enhancement Proposal process, requiring TC approval before implementation." "L3: Any changes made to the Governance process ... or any changes that impact the core protocol's scope or adoption, must be approved by Governance Council (GC)." "The TC reserves the right to stop any discussions deemed non-critical to the protocol."

Contributor licence [P]: "Contributions to this project must be accompanied by a Contributor License Agreement (CLA)." (Google CLA, https://cla.developers.google.com/). Signing a CLA is an action only the owner can take.

"Feature Request vs Enhancement Proposal" [P]: "For new feature suggestions without an implementation plan, please submit a standard \"Feature Request\" issue."

### 1.4 Route C: a Domain Working Group

Source [P]: `GOVERNANCE.md`

> "A group of 3+ organizations can submit a charter to the Governing Council to form a DWG (e.g., \"Travel WG\"). Once chartered, the DWG has autonomy to define capabilities for their domain and submit for DTC approvals."

> "Any DTC member can submit a DWG charter nomination (using the DWG charter template) as a new issue in the UCP Issues tracker." "GC reviews the DWG charter and approves or rejects the DWG nomination." "GC approves chairs/co-chairs for the DWG". "DWG chairs/co-chairs may invite additional industry participants to contribute to the DWG via the DWG charter issue."

> "DWG are subject to DTC oversight - all DWG artifacts must be reviewed and approved by the DTC."

Charter template sections [P] (`DOMAIN_WORKING_GROUP_CHARTER.md`): Problem Statement, Strategic Fit, Scope (In-Scope, Out-of-Scope), Key Deliverables, Deliver By, DTC Sponsors ("DTC name (e.g., Shopping DTC) and proposed Chairs/Co-Chairs").

So [I]: three organisations are needed, the nomination itself must be filed by a sitting Tech Council member, and the Governing Council approves. An individual cannot start one; he can be invited into one by its chairs.

Only existing example [P]: Bulk Product Discovery DWG, charter https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/682, "approved by the Governing Council on 2026-08-07", "Chairs / Co-Chairs: James Andersen (Meta), Vinod Kumar (Meta), Greg Smith (Google), Alex Jansen (Google)", "Target completion: late October 2026" (https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/meeting-minutes/blob/main/tc/shopping/dwg/bulk-product-discovery/README.md).

- GitHub Discussions, categories Announcements, General, Ideas, Polls, Q&A, Show and tell: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/discussions [P]

I could not find the address of that group in the README, the org profile, the contributing page or the minutes repository. Not confirmed that it exists publicly.
- UCP Summit: "32 participants have confirmed attendance for the upcoming Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) Summit in November" (minutes 2026-10-09 [P]). Invitations went to council members; no public registration found. Location not stated.

Criteria favour an organisation that "represents a large established ecosystem". Not a route for an individual.

## 3. WebMCP: who owns it and how to propose

### 3.1 The group and the process [P]

- Specification: "WebMCP, Draft Community Group Report, 9 October 2026". "Editors: Brandon Walderman (Microsoft), Khushal Sagar (Google), Dominic Farolino (Google)". "This specification was published by the Web Machine Learning Community Group. It is not a W3C Standard nor is it on the W3C Standards Track." https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/
- Repository: https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp (4,610 stars, 123 open issues and PRs, last push 9 Oct 2026). Issues: https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/issues
- Group: W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, https://www.w3.org/groups/cg/webmachinelearning/ . Chair: Anssi Kostiainen (W3C group page; affiliation Intel from his GitHub profile).
- Charter (start date 2025-09-25), https://webmachinelearning.github.io/charter/ : WebMCP API is "A Web API that allows web developers to expose their web application functionality as tools ... The API is designed for human-in-the-loop workflows where the user maintains visibility and remains in control." Decisions: "This group will seek to make decisions where there is consensus." "a decision should be publicly recorded (where GitHub is used as the resolution of an Issue)". Contributions "in the form of a pull request (preferred), by raising an issue, or by adding a comment to an existing issue."
- CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository: "This repository is being used for work in the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, governed by the W3C Community License Agreement (CLA). To make substantive contributions, you must join the CG."
- How to join (https://webmachinelearning.github.io/community/): "Create a W3C Account", "Join the Community Group", "If representing a W3C Member, also join the Working Group", "You're all set to contribute on GitHub and join meetings". Community Groups are free and open to individuals. Joining means creating an account, which only the owner can do.
- Meetings: Community Group teleconference every second Thursday, 15:00 to 16:00 UTC (agendas 3 Sep, 17 Sep, 1 Oct 2026 in https://github.com/webmachinelearning/meetings/tree/main/telcons; [I] next one 15 Oct 2026). Topics reach the agenda through the `Agenda+` label. Face to face: "W3C TPAC 2026: Web Machine Learning WG/CG F2F", Clayton Hotel Burlington Road, Dublin, "in-person & remote", 26 and 27 October 2026; "Submit agenda proposals via https://github.com/webmachinelearning/meetings/issues/39".
- Other channels: mailing list archive https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-webmachinelearning/ ; W3C Slack channel `#webmachinelearning`; IRC `#webmachinelearning`.
- Chrome side: "Raise questions and participate in discussion on GitHub." "If you have feedback on Chrome's implementation, file a Chromium bug." (https://crbug.com/new?component=2021259). "Join the early preview program (EPP) to provide feedback on WebMCP" (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/join-epp). Origin trial from Chrome 149.
- Edge side: "An Origin Trial is live in Edge 150." (implementation-status.md). Enrolling "requires that you agree to be contacted by Microsoft for feedback".
- Implementation status file also lists Brave (Leo), ChatGPT Desktop, Firefox and Safari positions, and Meta Ray-Ban Display ("coming soon").

How the editors treat outside ideas [P], Dominic Farolino, 28 Sep 2026: "implement it outside the spec, gather experience, and then file focused issues if that work reveals specific WebMCP primitives that are actually missing." (https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/issues/261#issuecomment-5875926859) and, same day, on an implementer note: "It doesn't seem like there's a concrete issue with the spec or API above though. ... Please file focused issues" (#266, "Implementation report: agent commerce storefront on WebMCP").

Relevant open issues: #31 "Support agent to agent interaction" (Khushal Sagar, 2025, no comments), #329 "Allow pages to send messages to agents" (30 Sep 2026), #188 "Tool retrieval: wildcard or not" (the hypothetical `tools.shopify.com` iframe), #8 "Should tools be a means for capability discovery?", #341 "Declarative tool-manifest for JS-callable tools" (12 Oct 2026), #340 "site guide for agents" (8 Oct 2026). On 8 Oct 2026 the declarative API was removed from the spec "for now" (commit by François Beaufort, #338).

### 3.2 Dominic Farolino (Google Chrome; WebMCP editor)
- Role [P]: "Editor: Dominic Farolino, Google" in the spec source and rendered spec (9 Oct 2026). GitHub bio: "Engineer @GoogleChrome. Ex-@microsoft @mozilla. Editor @whatwg." (profile updated 12 Oct 2026).

## 5. Public positions that a message can truthfully cite
1. UCP governance asks vendors to ship under their own namespace first and only then ask for core adoption (CONTRIBUTING.md).
2. The Shopping Tech Council recorded "strong industry demand for personalization, reordering, and upselling" when it discussed state-bound offers (2 Oct 2026).
3. The council admits outsiders "hit a wall" (4 Sep 2026) and deprioritises items "without an active implementer" (18 Sep 2026).
4. A Google engineer's proposal says "Commerce today is unidirectional in UCP" and adds a Buyer price proposal, but rules out non-price terms (11 Oct 2026).
5. Google's Direct Offers plans "bundles and free shipping" beyond discounts (11 Jan 2026) and promotions with advertiser "guardrails" assembled by Gemini (20 May 2026). The offer is chosen by Google from what the advertiser uploaded; it is not a reply to a buyer agent's stated priority or proof.
6. Press (7 Oct 2026): the Direct Offer asset uses single-use promo codes.
7. WebMCP editor: "All script running on your page is treated the same" (8 Apr 2026); new ideas should be built outside the spec first and come back as focused issues (28 Sep 2026).
8. A Google developer-relations engineer describes a website-side harness that "represents the business" meeting the user's agent (31 Aug 2026).
9. Amit Handa in public: "Contribute your feedback, extensions, and code to the public repository." (8 Sep 2026).

# G5 - Possible co-builders and allies for OfferAd ("build together something for this")

Research date: 13 Oct 2026. Every role below was confirmed from a page fetched today unless it says "unverified". Nobody was contacted; only read-only GETs of public pages, public GitHub API endpoints and the public Luma discover endpoint. No accounts, forms, posts, stars or follows. Raw copies of what I fetched are in `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/docs/g5/`.

Labels: `primary` = the person's or organisation's own page, profile, repository or official programme; `secondary` = press, aggregator or search summary; `unverified` = I could not confirm it today.

Scope reminder: this file covers builders and allies (companies already doing offers, negotiation or ads for shopping agents; independent open-source developers; Shopify discount/Functions studios; researchers; Bay Area venues). Shopify, Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Google executives and the protocol councils are other tasks' scope; they appear here only where they show up at a venue.

---

## 0. Short version

1. The single best venue is nine days away and local: **AGNTCon + MCPCon North America, 22 to 23 Oct 2026, San Jose McEnery Convention Center**. It has an Agentic Commerce track, a UCP panel with Ilya Grigorik (Shopify), Amit Handa and Greg Smith (Google) on Thu 22 Oct 4:40 PM, an open "Agentic Commerce" lunch table on Thu 22 Oct, and a talk by the independent author of `ucp-probe` on Fri 23 Oct. A one-day pass is $475, the Expo + Party pass $149.
2. The standards conversation OfferAd needs is happening in public this week, between individuals who answer newcomers within hours: UCP issue #738 (Arjun Garg, Intuit), discussion #502 (Chris Daly, I Want That!), discussion #863 (Yang W., StabileRewards, San Francisco, zero replies so far), issue #929 (Sparsh, Google London). On 9 Oct 2026 Arjun Garg asked in public for exactly what OfferAd can supply: "A concrete buyer proposal → seller counteroffer → Cart application → Checkout example".
3. Three small companies have hit the same wall (Shopify writes the store's UCP profile; apps cannot add to it) and said so in public: I Want That!, StabileRewards, Flux. They are competitors or complements in product and natural co-signers of one joint question to Shopify.
4. Two discount-Function studios are reachable by design and own the "one code, several effects" piece: Discount Kit (co-founders Sammy Isseyegh and Dave Spanton, UK; "The core team is always around for a chat") and Regios (Tobe Osakwe; "reach out. I read every message").
5. I found no agentic-commerce-specific meetup or hackathon in San Francisco dated November or December 2026. Three such events happened in the last eight weeks (23 Aug, 3 Oct, 5 Oct), so the organisers' calendars are the thing to watch.

His offers are buyer-initiated price offers; no competing-link verification and no seller-initiated non-price offer found.

- One ask: "Arjun asked on 9 Oct for a concrete buyer proposal → counteroffer → Cart → Checkout example; would you co-write it with me using a non-price counter (free express shipping) so the example covers more than price?"

Company classification, summary:

- **Competitors (same job on Shopify):** Flux (price haggling with agents; cross-store connector), I Want That! / Vector (customer- and agent-submitted offers). Neither verifies a competing link, and neither makes seller-initiated non-price offers.
- **Competitor with the opposite incentive:** ChatCast (commission to the agent operator).
- **Complements:** StabileRewards (next-order credit via agents), Facet (checkout and directory outside Shopify), ReFiBuy (catalog optimisation), Nekuda and MCP-B (WebMCP tooling), Talon.One (enterprise promotions with UCP extensions), competitor-price trackers on the App Store (Prisync, Price Parrot, PriceOtus: they monitor competitor prices for merchants; none verifies a buyer-supplied link, per their listings' descriptions).
- **Possible partners for the settlement layer:** Discount Kit, Regios (also on the App Store: SupaEasy by Nextools, Function Studio, Function Junction, Kite; not researched to person level).
- **Possible partner as a proving ground:** Shopware Agentic Commerce Lab (a platform where a vendor extension can enter the store profile).
- Fresh App Store searches today ("price match", "competitor price match", "ai agent offers", "agent discount", "agentic offers") returned no new app that makes offers to buyer agents beyond those in R6, and no app that verifies a competitor link.

### 3.2 UCP GitHub Discussions and the four live threads

- `primary`: the UCP README lists one community channel: "Questions & Discussions: Join our GitHub Discussions" - https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/discussions . I found no community call, Slack or Discord in the README; CONTRIBUTING.md returned 404 at the path I tried.
- Threads: #502 "A Buyer's Agent Should Negotiate" (Ideas; 4 comments, 6 replies); #738 Offer extension (updated 10 Oct 2026); #863 platform-hosted profiles (0 comments); #929 Quote extension (opened 11 Oct 2026); #384 Provider + offer discovery.

# OfferAd outreach plan (editor-in-chief ranking)

Date: 13 Oct 2026. Built from the five researched groups (G1 Shopify, G2 Meta/Sierra/Stripe, G3 OpenAI/xAI/others, G4 Google/WebMCP/UCP, G5 builders and allies) and their adversarial verifications in this folder (`V-G1` to `V-G5`). Only people whose role survived verification (confirmed or corrected) are ranked. Unverified but important people are in tier 2 with the caveat. Dropped people are listed with the reason.

Operating rules for the owner (one person, a working prototype, no audience):

- He sends everything himself. Nobody here has contacted anyone.
- He is a software engineer in San Francisco building a side project. Never "founder".
- Public professional channels only; no guessed addresses; personal Gmail addresses visible on GitHub profiles (Amit Handa, Arjun Garg, Lee Richmond) are not used.
- Every quoted hook below was fetched today or re-verified by the verification pass; where a quote is a minute-taker's paraphrase or a co-signed post, it is labelled.

## 0. What the plan is for

Three missing pieces that only other people can supply:

- (a) Shopify letting an installed app contribute to the store's agent surface (an app-defined tool or UCP extension, an agents.md section, or `context.intent` / `context.eligibility` reaching a Discount Function).
- (b) Agent makers (Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots/ChatGPT, xAI Grok Bot, Perplexity, Google) letting their agents call a seller's offer endpoint or listing an offer connector.
- (c) Protocol groups (UCP, PAP, ACP, WebMCP) adding an offer or reconsideration-offer message.

The single most important finding across all five groups: **the offer message is already on the UCP Shopping Tech Council's table.** Issue #738 (state-bound Offer, outside author Arjun Garg) is on the 2026-12-08 milestone, assigned to Greg Smith (Google), and was debated on 2 Oct 2026; the council said on 18 Sep 2026 that "items without an active implementer behind them are a signal to deprioritize". Issue #929 (Quote extension with a buyer price proposal, Google engineer Sparsh, 11 Oct 2026) is the buyer-initiated half and its checklist asks for "implementer evidence". A live Shopify app that does exactly this is the evidence both threads are missing. That is why the plan starts in those two GitHub threads, not with a note to a CEO.

## 1. Tier 1 (eight people)

Criteria: (a) owns or strongly influences a missing piece, (b) a short note or public comment from an unknown builder has a realistic chance of being read, (c) there is a concrete small ask. Reply odds are rough ranges with reasoning. Where the "channel" is a public GitHub comment, the note is the comment.

### 1.1 Arjun Garg - author of UCP Offer extension #738 / PR #773 (outside contributor)

- Role (verified): author of `[Proposal]: State-bound Offer extension for merchant-proposed Cart changes` (opened 15 Aug 2026, updated 10 Oct 2026), PR #773, #845, draft PR #918. `author_association` NONE: not a maintainer. GitHub profile says company "Intuit"; self-declared only, so do not state it in a message. Source: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/738 and https://github.com/arjun2075 (fetched 13 Oct 2026).
- Why this person: he writes the text the council is weighing for December. He asked in public, four days ago, for exactly what OfferAd can supply.
- What he controls: the scope, wording and examples of the only offer proposal with a milestone; he does not control adoption (the council does).
- The ask: "Would a worked example on #738 help: buyer priority and competing-offer link in, state-bound offer out, settled on Shopify as a single-use discount code and cart link, plus a test vector backed by a real code?"
- Hook (his own words, 9 Oct 2026, https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/738#issuecomment-6087028190): "A concrete buyer proposal → seller counteroffer → Cart application → Checkout example would be useful for identifying which parts #738 can cover and which belong in the negotiation/handoff work." Same comment: "#738 currently represents a Business-proposed Cart transition; it doesn't define those negotiation states or arbitrary changes to shipping, payment terms, or other commercial conditions."
- Channel: one comment on issue #738. No other published channel.
- Better route: none; the thread is the route.
- Reply odds: 70-90%. He has answered every comment in the thread within a day, thanked a first-time reviewer and changed the PR the same day (28 Aug 2026), and the ask is one he made himself.
- Confidence in role: 0.85.

## 3. Venues: where filing beats a personal note

### 3.1 UCP issue #738 (state-bound Offer) - first action

- URL: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/738 (PR #773)
- What to file: one comment, under 300 words, structured as the worked example Arjun Garg asked for on 9 Oct: (1) buyer agent request: priority (e.g. "fastest delivery") plus competing-offer URL; (2) seller verification of the link and the answer: a state-bound offer with a non-price term (free express shipping) and an expiry; (3) settlement on Shopify: single-use discount code submitted through the documented `discounts.codes` field, with a cart link; (4) a link to a public demo store and the `com.offerad.*` schema served from the owner's domain; (5) one question: which of this belongs in #738 and which in #929 or the negotiation/handoff work. @-mention @gsmith85 and @arjun2075. Do not pitch; do not mention competitors.
- Exact steps: read the full thread first (Chris Daly and Weston have commented; Arjun asked Daly a follow-up on 10 Oct). Post from the owner's GitHub account. No CLA is needed to comment; a Google CLA is needed only for a pull request. Then watch the Shopping Tech Council minutes (next file expected 16 Oct 2026) for the outcome.

### 3.2 UCP issue #929 (Quote extension, buyer price proposal)

- URL: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/issues/929 (draft PR #930)
- What to file: one comment with implementer evidence: the gap (no evidence link, no non-price priority) and how a Shopify-side implementation settles the accepted price. Cross-link to the #738 comment. Reviewer tagged by the author: Jing Li (Google, Shopping Tech Council).

### 3.3 UCP discussions #863 and #502

- URLs: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/discussions/863 (how a third-party app reaches a Shopify-hosted profile; 0 replies since 25 Sep 2026) and https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp/discussions/502 ("A Buyer's Agent Should Negotiate").
- What to file: in #863, add the OfferAd case under Yang W.'s question so the question to Shopify carries two apps. In #502, a reply to Juan Fernández (Shopware) and Chris Daly linking the #738 example. Later: a "Show and tell" post for the `com.offerad.*` vendor extension once it is live.

### 3.6 Personal Agent Protocol: feedback on draft 0.1 and design-partner request

- URL: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/path-to-1
- What to file: a review in the format the site asks for: title "Review of the Personal Agent Protocol docs (2026-10-12)", a 2-3 sentence summary, points grouped by section id (extensions-operations#revisions, spec#extensions, General), each labelled Gap / Ambiguous / Contradiction / Risk / Wording / Question with a suggested fix. The point: Operations covers company-proposed terms with revisions and expiry but has no way for a company to propose a conditional offer in response to a stated priority or proof; propose it as a "broadly useful extension". Email it to the feedback address printed on the page ([EMAIL REDACTED]). In the same mail, request design-partner status as a technology provider (the page asks for a technical and a partnership contact; it neither admits nor excludes individuals).
- Caution: feedback is licensed to all members and users, perpetual and royalty-free. There is no public repo, tracker, mailing list or named editor. Design workshops were promised "over the next month" (9 Oct 2026) with no date yet.

### 3.7 ACP: Reconsideration Offers SEP

- URL: https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol/blob/main/docs/sep-guidelines.md ; the hook text is in https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol/blob/main/rfcs/rfc.intent_traces.md ("A subsequent RFC MAY define **Reconsideration Offers** keyed to specific reason codes.")
- What to file: first ask Tomas Taylor (section 4) whether he is writing it. If not: a GitHub Issue tagged SEP and proposal with preamble, ~200-word abstract, motivation, specification (a minimal offer response keyed to `reason_code`, with expiry and redemption), rationale, backward compatibility, reference implementation, security. Then one Ideas Discussion asking for a sponsor (seats: OpenAI aravindrao-openai, Stripe prasad-stripe, Meta lhwa; two of three needed; OpenAI and Stripe hold vetoes).
- Cautions: no commit on main since 18 Jul 2026; 144 open issues; recent SEPs unlabelled and unassigned; unsponsored proposals may be closed as dormant after three months. Governance forbids "product marketing or self-promotion" and "direct comparisons between competing products" in ACP channels. A pull request needs OpenAPI and JSON Schema under spec/unreleased/, a changelog file and a signed individual CLA. Treat ACP as the third protocol, not the first.

- URLs: https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/issues ; join at https://www.w3.org/community/webmachinelearning/join ; demos at https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/webmcp-tools ; TPAC agenda issue https://github.com/webmachinelearning/meetings/issues/39

TPAC 2026 is in Dublin on 26-27 Oct (remote attendance possible); the WebMCP day is reported as Tue 27 Oct; propose a five-minute implementer report on issue #39 only after the focused issue exists.

### 3.11 Muse: connector submission and custom connector demo

- URLs: https://muse.ai/platform (reviewed directory) and the custom-connector route described at https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/
- What to do: (1) today: use a Muse custom connector pointed at the OfferAd endpoint to record a demo (Meta does not review these; it is a demo route, not distribution); (2) when the connector satisfies the rules, submit through "Submit a connector" with overview, business verification, data questionnaire, endpoint/auth and tool docs labelled read/write/sensitive-write, and a test account. Rules that bite: 1.1 a connector that only sends the user to checkout fails the completion rule; 3.2 tools must not steer Muse away from competitors or force recommendations; 4.3 advertising and sponsored results must be labelled and discounts must be real; 5.7 Meta does not answer status messages. The terms page returned HTTP 400, so fees and eligibility for individuals are unknown.

### 3.12 OpenAI plugin portal and developer forum

- URLs: https://platform.openai.com/plugins ; https://community.openai.com (category "ChatGPT Apps SDK"); guidelines https://developers.openai.com/plugins/plugin-guidelines.md
- What to file: one forum question quoting the Advertising rule ("Plugins must not serve advertisements and must not exist primarily as an advertising vehicle.") and the pass-through rule, describing an offer-returning tool, and asking which side of the line it falls. Then submit a per-merchant plugin (safer than a cross-store broker) after individual verification; appeal by replying to a rejection email. Guidelines also require external checkout on the merchant's domain and allow commerce only for physical goods.

### 3.15 UCP Domain Working Group (the literal "build together" mechanism, later)

- URL: https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/DOMAIN_WORKING_GROUP_CHARTER.md
- Rule: "A group of 3+ organizations can submit a charter to the Governing Council to form a DWG"; the nomination is filed by a Tech Council member; chairs "may invite additional industry participants". An individual cannot start one but can be invited. Embiricos's title differs across three press sources; use the product name. Amit Handa's "Director of Engineering" is from January 2026. Daniel Wyckoff, Lee Richmond, Yoav Weiss, Greg Smith, James Andersen, Lee Hwa, Prasad Wangikar, Aravind Rao, Patrick Jordan: council seats confirmed, job titles not; do not state titles for them.
- Arjun Garg's Intuit affiliation is self-declared on GitHub; do not state it. Yang W. is in Dublin, CA, not San Francisco. Tomas Taylor may be in New York, not San Francisco. Moretto is not confirmed independent.
- Do not address Carl Rivera, Lilian Rincon, Holly Li, Nayna Sheth or Ginny Marvin as current owners of anything.

Quotes that must be labelled:

- Ilya Grigorik's 2 Oct 2026 remark is the minute-taker's paraphrase; the same minute lists him as confirming demand. Never say he opposed offers. Greg Smith's 18 Sep "signal to deprioritize" line is also a minutes paraphrase.
- Wes's "known gap" is about fulfilment details in the UCP profile, not offers.
- Kulikowski's 31 Aug post is co-written with Idan Levin and André Bandarra. Clay Bavor's and Gram Liu's quotes are co-signed company posts. Sottiaux's quote is a third-party machine transcript.
- Singleton's partner list is not the PAP membership (Decagon is not on the site's design-partner list).
- Jiaxin Pei's "please reach out" is about his course, not negotiation research.

Policies that can forbid the ask:

- OpenAI plugin guidelines ban plugins that "serve advertisements", "exist primarily as an advertising vehicle" or are "pass-through intermediary software layers"; a cross-store broker plugin is at risk, a per-merchant plugin less so. Commerce only for physical goods; external checkout on the merchant's domain.
- Muse connector rules 1.1 (must complete the task, not hand off to checkout), 3.2 (no steering away from competitors or forcing recommendations), 4.3 (label advertising; discounts must be real), 5.7 (no status replies). Terms page unavailable; fees and individual eligibility unknown.
- Anthropic directory policy 4.C excludes advertising and sponsored content "unless otherwise expressly permitted".
- ACP governance forbids product marketing, self-promotion and competitor comparisons in its channels; every SEP needs a TSC sponsor; the repo has been quiet since 18 Jul 2026.
- UCP CONTRIBUTING.md: vendor namespace (`com.offerad.*`, schema served from the matching domain) first; a core Enhancement Proposal only after "proven widespread adoption". Comments need no CLA; pull requests need a Google CLA.
- WebMCP editors close general implementation reports (#266, 28 Sep 2026); only narrow spec questions survive.
- PAP feedback is licensed perpetual and royalty-free to all members and users.
- Cursor Marketplace requires open-source plugins and works with "a small group of trusted partners". Perplexity's form is for companies. Stripe Startups Build Day (11 Nov) is for "venture-backed founders"; a side-project engineer may be declined.

Things that could embarrass the owner:

- Calling himself a founder, or OfferAd a company, anywhere; he is a software engineer with a side project.
- Pitching in a spec thread. Every GitHub comment must be an implementer report or a question, with no product name in the title and no competitor comparisons.
- Sending Flux (a direct competitor) the link-verification or non-price design.
- Claiming Shopify "blocked" apps from the agent surface as a quote; staff said "developers can't add to or adjust a merchant's /.well-known/ucp endpoint" (Wes, 21 Aug 2026) and "there's no extension point for custom product fields or custom checkout logic through the MCP tools themselves" (Kyle Giesbrecht, 28 Jul 2026); quote those.
- Shopify is building its own paid layer (Promoted placements, Shop Campaigns in ChatGPT) and Google its own Direct Offers; frame OfferAd as a seller-side answer to a buyer agent's stated priority, not as "ads in agents", which both platforms reserve for themselves.
- Using personal Gmail addresses visible on GitHub profiles (Amit Handa, Arjun Garg, Lee Richmond) or Singleton's agent-only address. Never guess an email.
- The Cheeky Pint interview that sources Wang's quote is hosted by Stripe's John Collison; cite it as an interview page, not as Meta.
- X profile timelines could not be read in date order today; a newer post than the ones quoted may exist for each person. Re-read the target's latest posts and MAINTAINERS.md immediately before sending anything.

# V-G1 - Adversarial verification of G1-shopify (Shopify people)

Verification date: 13 Oct 2026. Verifier's own fetches, all read-only GETs of public pages. Nobody was contacted; nothing was posted, starred, followed, signed up for or submitted.

Raw copies of what I fetched are in the session scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/vg1/`), not in the project folder.

## How each source was read

- Web pages (dotdev.shopify.com, shopify.com newsroom and investor pages, ilya.grigorik.com, gilgreenberg.com, blog.yoav.ws, danielwyckoff.ca, sierra.ai, techcrunch.com, pymnts.com, fs.blog, productschool.com, stackoverflow.blog, channelnews.com.au, retailgentic.transistor.fm): `curl` with a browser User-Agent, text extracted locally, quoted strings searched in the text.
- GitHub (profiles, MAINTAINERS.md and its commit history, council minutes, pull requests, issues, discussions): `gh api -X GET`.
- Shopify developer forum: public Discourse JSON (`/t/<id>.json`, `/u/<name>.json`, `/search.json`).
- X posts: the public embed endpoint `cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result?id=<id>` (three posts verified).
- X profile bios: the embed profile endpoint returned 429 (rate limit) all session. Bios were read through the public FixTweet mirror `api.fxtwitter.com/<handle>` (a third-party mirror of public X profile data; flaky, several handles needed retries) and cross-checked against the researcher's saved raw copies in `work/docs/g1/x/`. Label for these: "X bio, read 13 Oct 2026 through a mirror".
- LinkedIn: not fetched. Every LinkedIn URL below comes from the person's own site, X profile or a podcast page.

## 1. Gil Greenberg - CORRECTED

Claimed: "Staff Product Manager, agentic commerce (checkout, Functions in agentic checkouts, checkout WebMCP); UCP Shopping Tech Council member since 15 Sep 2026".

What I checked and found:

- DotDev lineup, https://dotdev.shopify.com/pages/sessions (event 21-22 Jul 2026): "How Shopify Functions help you succeed in agentic checkouts ... Gil Greenberg | Staff Product Manager | Shopify". Found.
- UCP MAINTAINERS.md (raw file read today): Shopping Tech Council row "Gil Greenberg | Shopify". Commit history: 2026-09-15 "docs(maintainers): replace Victoria Duggan with Gil Greenberg on Shopping Tech Council (#71)". Found. He is listed as present in the 9 Oct 2026 minutes (not in the 2 Oct minutes, when offers were discussed).
- His site https://www.gilgreenberg.com/ : "Hey! I'm based in NYC and work at Shopify as a Product lead." and "In NYC? Reach out on social media and I'd be happy to grab a coffee (I respond best on Twitter)." Found. The site links to twitter.com/gilgnyc, linkedin.com/in/gilgreenberg and github.com/gil--, so all three channels are his.
- GitHub `gil--`: name "Gil Greenberg", company "@shopify", twitter_username "gilgnyc", profile updated 2026-10-12. Public member of the Shopify organisation.
- X bio @gilgNYC (mirror, 13 Oct 2026): "Agentic commerce @Shopify. Try it at http://UCP.new  Prev: @checkoutblocks (acq by Shopify)".
- X post 2104583942728822998 (embed endpoint): created 2026-09-28T14:48:07Z by gilgNYC. Text matches the quote; the original has a yawning emoji after "paint dry." that the researcher dropped. The link goes to an X article.
- Press: TechCrunch 28 Sep 2026: "Gil Greenberg, a staff product manager who works on agentic commerce at Shopify". PYMNTS 28 Sep 2026: "Gil Greenberg, staff product manager, checkout at Shopify, wrote in a Monday (Sept. 28) article on LinkedIn". The two press titles disagree on the team.

New evidence the researcher did not have:

1. The forum account `Gil-Shopify` is provably Gil Greenberg. His posts are signed. Thread 35930 (9 Jul 2026) and thread 29264 (4 Feb 2026) both end: "Gil Greenberg Product Manager, Checkout". The researcher wrote "same person not proven"; that caveat can be removed.
2. He appears to have changed teams in September 2026. In thread 35930, post 20, 16 Sep 2026, a developer (Alex Hooper) wrote: "@Gil-Shopify do you know who'll be taking this on now you're moving teams?" Nobody answered. This is a third party's remark, not Gil's own statement, but it lines up with the council seat of 15 Sep 2026 and with his X bio now reading "Agentic commerce @Shopify" while his July signature said "Product Manager, Checkout".
3. He is active on UCP GitHub: he authored PR #793 "feat(permalink): add ucp/version protocol version parameter" (updated 13 Oct 2026) and left review comments on 7 and 9 Oct 2026.

Corrected role: Staff Product Manager at Shopify, now working on agentic commerce (UCP Shopping Tech Council since 15 Sep 2026; announced checkout WebMCP on 28 Sep 2026; answers Checkout MCP threads). Until at least 9 Jul 2026 he signed as "Product Manager, Checkout". The move itself rests on a third party's remark plus his own bio.

What is wrong or inflated in the researcher's entry:

- "Closest verified owner of 'context.intent or context.eligibility into Discount Functions'" is too strong. His July work was checkout validation Functions and the buyer journey intercept; the Discount Function API belongs to the Discounts team (forum: Adam Ford, "Developer from the Discounts team here", 13 Aug 2026). After the reported team move, whoever inherited checkout extensibility is unnamed. He is, however, now closer to the other half of missing piece (a): the store's agent surface (UCP, Checkout MCP, checkout WebMCP).
- The 9 Jul quote "I'd love to hear about any use cases you're blocked on, what we're missing" was an invitation about the buyer journey intercept deprecation, written in his old role. It is still fair to cite, with that context.

Channels (all verified as his): X https://x.com/gilgNYC ; GitHub https://github.com/gil-- ; site https://www.gilgreenberg.com/ ; LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/in/gilgreenberg (linked from his site; not fetched); forum https://community.shopify.dev/u/Gil-Shopify .

# V-G2: adversarial check of G2 (Meta, Sierra, Stripe)

Checked on 13 Oct 2026. Every source below was fetched by me today unless marked otherwise. Nobody was contacted; nothing was posted, followed, starred or submitted. All fetches were anonymous reads of public pages.

Labels: **[P]** primary (organisation's own page, the person's own profile or post, a maintainer file). **[S]** secondary (press, conference bio). **[snippet]** search-result summary only. **[inferred]** my reading.

How things were read:
- Web pages: `curl` with a browser User-Agent, text extracted locally, quoted strings searched for literally.
- X posts: the public embed endpoint (`cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result`). It returns author, date, counts and the first ~280 characters. Profile bios could not be read (the profile endpoint returned 429 all session).
- GitHub: the REST API was rate-limited (0 of 60 left), so I used public HTML profile pages and the public `.atom` commit feeds instead.
- LinkedIn: the logged-out public profile page loaded (HTTP 200) for most people and shows name, employer, location, follower count and recent public posts. Job titles are masked with asterisks on that view. Post dates are relative ("6d", "2w"), so dates derived from them are approximate.

## 1. Overall verdict

The researcher's list is mostly sound. No wrong person, no one who has left, no fabricated quote. Every quoted sentence I checked is on the cited page, word for word. The faults are of three kinds:

1. **Stale or weaker evidence than exists.** Jeff Weinstein's and Steve Kaliski's titles were cited from a 29 Sep 2025 page; Stripe printed both again on 18 Mar 2026. Kaliski's "Principal Software Engineer" is on Stripe's own Sessions 2026 speaker list, not only a conference bio.
2. **Channels and statements missed.** Prasad Wangikar, James Andersen, Clay Bavor, Bret Taylor, Kevin Miller and Steve Kaliski all have verifiable public LinkedIn profiles; Wangikar and Andersen link theirs from their own GitHub profiles. Wangikar and Kaliski both made first-person public statements on agent shopping in the last three weeks. Weinstein publishes a contact address himself. Bret Taylor publicly invited people to ask him about joining PAP.
3. **"Controls" claims that go beyond the evidence.** "Singleton controls whether Muse lists an extension" and "Wang controls the organisation that builds Muse" are inferences. What is evidenced: Singleton is Meta's named spokesperson on PAP; Wang is Chief AI Officer of MSL; the Muse product team is described by Zuckerberg as "Nat's team".

Verdict counts: 9 confirmed, 3 corrected (Wangikar, Kaliski, Weinstein), 0 unverified, 0 drop.

## 2. Person by person

### Alexandr Wang (Meta) - CONFIRMED
- **Role quote checked [S]:** "Mark Zuckerberg (founder and CEO, Meta) and Alexandr Wang (Chief AI Officer, Meta Superintelligence Labs) join John for a pint to discuss the launch of Muse Wonder and the future of personal AI agents." https://cheekypint.substack.com/p/muse-wonder-zuckerberg-and-wangs (page metadata `datePublished` 2026-10-12T19:26:48Z). Present, exact.
- **Supporting [S]:** CNBC 8 Sep 2026 "Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang"; TechCrunch 22 Sep 2026 "Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang". Both re-fetched and present.
- **Statement checked:** "I think Muse is one of the first products where you're actually people are fully delegating purchases to the agents." Present in the transcript under the speaker label "Alexandr Wang". The next sentences are also usable: "we've been talking a lot about agentic shopping and like the possibility of it, but now it's like really happening."
- **Channel:** X `@alexandr_wang`. Embed data shows name "Alexandr Wang", verified, affiliation label "Meta". His.
- **Reply counts:** 24 Sep 2026 post (id 2102915571276992875): 358 replies, 6,589 likes today. Matches.
- **Anything newer that contradicts:** none found. An interview dated yesterday still uses the title.
- **Issues:**
  - No Meta-owned page states the title (Meta's executive gallery returned HTTP 400 for me too). The role stays "confirmed by an interview page and press".
  - March 2026 press (Storyboard18, 6 Mar 2026, summarising other reports) [S] says Meta reorganised: "some engineering teams, data pipelines and model oversight responsibilities that were previously part of the broader AI structure have been reassigned" and a new applied AI engineering organisation was set up under Maher Saba. So "controls the organisation that builds Muse" is broader than the evidence. Wikipedia's MSL page [S] lists the product group as "Products and Applied Research: Led by Friedman". Whether Friedman reports to Wang in 2026 is unverified, as the researcher said.
  - The Substack is John Collison's (Stripe). A note that cites it is citing a Stripe co-founder's show, which is fine but worth knowing.

### Nat Friedman (Meta) - CONFIRMED (press only)
- **Role quote checked [S]:** "According to an X post by Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta's Superintelligence Labs (MSL), Muse was "definitely heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw."" https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/22/meta-admits-muses-likeness-to-openclaw-isnt-a-coincidence/ (`datePublished` 2026-09-22). Present.
- **Primary support checked:** Zuckerberg in the 12 Oct transcript: "whether they're the people in the lab who are working on that or the people on Nat's team who are working on the product". Present. Friedman's own X reply of 21 Sep 2026 (id 2102103707936768130): "After I used openclaw in january I bought hundreds of mac minis for the MSL team". Present.
- **Statement checked:** X, 2 Oct 2026 19:09 UTC (id 2106099383037309211): "Announcing Muse Gadgets, an open source ESP32 firmware and Linux sdk so that you can make hardware devices that work with Muse." Present; 411 replies, 7,167 likes. It is about a hardware SDK, not commerce. I also found no statement by him on offers, ads or shopping agents.
- **Channels:** X `@natfriedman` (name "Nat Friedman", verified; no Meta affiliation label, unlike Wang and Zuckerberg). https://nat.org/ re-fetched: no employer, no contact address. Both his.
- **Issues:**
  - Title is press-only. Wikipedia [S] also says "currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs"; a search summary mentioned a variant "VP of Product and Applied Research" [snippet]. Treat the exact wording as press usage.
  - "He did answer a small app builder in public" overstates it. The 21 Sep reply was to a viral post (TechCrunch: "a post that had gone viral among the AI crowd") that accused Muse of copying OpenClaw. That is damage control on a trending thread, not evidence that he answers cold notes from builders.

### David Singleton (Meta) - CONFIRMED (and strengthened)
- **Role quote checked [S]:** "David Singleton, Meta's Superintelligence Labs vice president of engineering and consumer products, said in an interview with CNBC." Present at the cited URL, which redirects to https://siliconangle.com/2026/10/06/meta-teams-up-with-bret-taylors-sierra-technologies-on-new-standards-for-ai-agent-commerce/ (`datePublished` 2026-10-07T00:54Z, i.e. 6 Oct US time).
- **Original found (researcher could not):** CNBC, 6 Oct 2026 [S]: "David Singleton, vice president of engineering and consumer products at Meta Superintelligence Labs and former technology chief at Stripe, highlighted security." https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/meta-joins-companies-to-tame-chaos-of-doing-business-with-ai-bots.html
- **Primary found:** his own LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/in/davidpsingleton/, linked from his about page) has page title "David Singleton - Meta", San Francisco Bay Area, 43K followers. His own post there (shown as "6mo"; press dates the deal 23-24 Mar 2026): "Excited to announce that Hugo Barra, Nicholas Jitkoff and I are joining Meta Superintelligence Labs with the entire Dreamer team today." SiliconANGLE 23 Mar 2026 [S] says the team works "within Meta's Superintelligence Labs group under Chief AI Officer ... Alexandr Wang, according to a report in Bloomberg".
- **Statement checked:** X, 6 Oct 2026 20:17 UTC (id 2107565831257567324), exact as quoted; 15 replies, 216 likes. A fuller first-person version is on his LinkedIn (about 6-7 Oct 2026, 18 comments): "Email as a means of communicating took off because everyone agreed on addressing, delivery and bounces. No one owns it and anyone can build on it. We believe agent commerce will work the same way, which is why we want to define these rails together."
- **Channels:** X `@dps` (linked from both his about page and his GitHub profile), GitHub `dps` (name "David Singleton"), LinkedIn, https://blog.singleton.io/ . All his. The `[EMAIL REDACTED]` address is on his about page and is explicitly "For AI agents"; I agree it should not be used for a person-to-person note.
- **Issues:**
  - His partner list ("Genesys, NiCE, Decagon, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart") differs from Sierra's ("Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart"). Decagon is not on the design-partner list at personalagentprotocol.org/docs/path-to-1 as of today. The quote is accurate, but a draft message should not repeat his list as the membership.
  - "Controls Meta's side of PAP, and so whether Muse lists a given extension" is inferred. Evidence supports "Meta's named spokesperson on PAP", nothing about who decides extension support.
  - Useful fact the researcher only had as a snippet: he was Stripe's technology chief (CNBC and SiliconANGLE, both fetched).

### Lee Hwa (Meta) - CONFIRMED (seat only)
- **Role quote checked [P]:** `| 3    | Meta        | lhwa              |` under "Current TSC Members" in `docs/governance.md` on `main`. The commit feed for that file shows the row's commit: 2026-04-24T16:44:27Z, author `lhwa`, "ADMIN: Add Meta as TSC member (#236)". No later commit to the file.

# V-G4: adversarial verification of G4 (Google, WebMCP, UCP governance)

Checked on 13 Oct 2026. Nobody was contacted. Nothing was posted, starred, followed or signed up for. Only read-only fetches: the public GitHub API (`gh api`, GET only), `curl` of public pages, the fetch tool for pages that return 403 to curl (w3.org), and web search.

Input checked: `/Users/mustafatokmak/.herdr-projects/offerad/threads/t-0006/work/people/G4-google-webmcp-ucp.md`

Labels: **[P]** primary source I fetched today. **[S]** press or a search snippet. **[I]** my inference.

---

## 0. Result in short

- 17 people checked. 16 roles hold up against the cited source. 1 (Ginny Marvin) could not be confirmed as current: newest primary source is 28 Jan 2026, newest press is 11 Jun 2026.
- No wrong person, no namesake confusion, no departed person in the list. Every quoted sentence I looked for is on the cited page, word for word.
- Real errors found (all in the "activity" claims, not in the roles):
  1. **Khushal Sagar**: G4 says no public statement in the last six months, latest 14 Jan 2026. Wrong. He commented in the WebMCP repository on 12 Jun, 26 Jun and 6 Jul 2026.
  2. **Brandon Walderman**: G4 says his latest repository comment is from 2 Mar 2026. Wrong. He has 23 issue comments since 1 Apr 2026, the latest on 6 Aug 2026.
  3. **Amit Handa, suggested ask**: the ask "is the draft shopping roadmap available" is already answered in the minutes of 25 Sep 2026: the council decided to publish the roadmap as GitHub milestone links. #738 is on milestone `2026-12-08`; #929 is on no milestone.
  4. **Kulikowski quote**: the 31 Aug 2026 post is co-authored ("Coauthored with Idan Levin · Nekuda", "Coauthored with André Bandarra · Google"). The sentence is real but it is not his alone.
  5. **Vidhya Srinivasan**: G4 missed her own bylined letter of 11 Feb 2026, which has a better Direct Offers sentence than the 11 Jan one. Still older than six months.
  6. **Sam Dallstream, "controls"**: "how Copilot in Edge uses page tools" is not supported. The only Microsoft statement on that is Walderman, 31 Jul 2026: "We don't have any links to share about in-browser Copilot integration at this time."
  7. **UCP Summit date**: G4 lists it as not confirmed. The minutes of 25 Sep 2026 give it: "the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) Summit on November 11–12, 2026". The minutes of 18 Sep 2026 say "The initial invitation covers Shopping Tech Council maintainers and public contributors". City still not stated.
- Role-staleness trap avoided by G4 but worth recording: **Lilian Rincon**, the former Google VP of Consumer Shopping Product, is reported [S, search snippet of Reuters/MediaPost/Yahoo Finance, March 2026] to have left for Apple as VP of AI product marketing. Do not address her as Google. Her successor on the buyer-agent side of Google Shopping was not identified. That is the largest gap in this scope: nobody on the list controls whether Google's own shopping agents call a seller's offer endpoint.

---

## 1. UCP and Google people

### 1.1 Greg Smith: CONFIRMED
- [P] `MAINTAINERS.md`, Shopping Tech Council table: `| Greg Smith      | Google     |`. https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md . - [P] "co-leads its weekly meeting": minutes headers read "Led by: Greg Smith" (4 Sep), "Led by: Amit Handa, Greg Smith" (18 Sep), "Led by: Greg Smith, Amit Handa" (25 Sep, 2 Oct), "Led by: Amit Handa" (9 Oct; Smith not in the attendance list).
